items.answer_should_show: Two card squares folded together at the hinge, with the band running round the outside of the fold from notch to notch, and arrows showing the band pulling the cards to open flat.

items.question: Draw a comic strip in four boxes: energy going into a store, waiting, and coming out later. Use any store from this unit.
items.answer_should_show: For example: 1. A child rolls the jar 3 turns. 2. The child holds it still and counts to 60. 3. The child lets go. 4. The jar rolls back. Each box has a label: in, waiting, out.

items.question: Draw a ball bouncing three times, each bounce lower than the last. Mark where some of the energy goes each time the ball touches the floor.
items.answer_should_show: A ball path with three bounces getting lower, and small wavy lines or arrows at the floor for heat and sound.

items.question: Draw an energy chain from the Sun to a child kicking a football. Label each store along the way.
items.answer_should_show: The Sun, then a plant, then food, then the child's muscles, then the football's movement.

items.question: Draw the bathroom floor from your rain test. Draw an arrow to show where the wrapper went. Draw a circle round the thing that stayed.
items.answer_should_show: An arrow from the wrapper to the drain, and a circle round the pebble.

items.question: Draw the journey of a toffee wrapper dropped on your road: from a hand, along the road in the rain, to where it ends up.
items.answer_should_show: A drawing with a hand, the road with rain, a drain, and maybe a river or the sea, with arrows between them.

items.question: Draw a bin for a windy balcony that the wind cannot empty. Show how it keeps the litter in.
items.answer_should_show: For example, a bin with a lid and a stone on top, or a narrow slot to push litter through.

items.question: Draw the four loops after the wet loop test. Show which ones tore and which stayed whole.
items.answer_should_show: A drawing with the wet paper loop torn, and the dry paper, cloth and plastic loops whole. The plastic loop may look stretched.

items.question: In the bag-in-the-bucket test, a thin bag drifted in the water. Draw a sea turtle seeing a floating bag and a jellyfish side by side.
items.answer_should_show: A drawing of a turtle with a puffed-open bag and a jellyfish that look alike.

items.question: Draw the closed box from the Closed Box Test. Draw arrows to show where the water went: from the cotton, into the air, onto the lid and back down.
items.answer_should_show: A box with cotton and seedlings, arrows going up from the cotton and the leaves, drops on the lid, and arrows going back down to the cotton.

items.question: Draw your window. Draw and label two living things and two non-living things you can see from it.
items.answer_should_show: A drawing of the window with four labelled things, two living (for example a crow and a tree) and two non-living (for example a road and the sun).

items.question: Draw a peepal growing out of a crack in an old wall. Draw how their roots change the wall over many years.
items.answer_should_show: A wall with a crack, a peepal sapling, and roots pushing into the crack, making it wider, with a few bricks loose.

items.question: Draw a picture of the Earth as a closed box. Show the sunlight coming in, heat going out, and water going round between sea, cloud, rain and river.
items.answer_should_show: The Earth with arrows of sunlight coming in, wavy arrows of heat going out to space, and a loop of arrows for water.

items.question: Draw one cut wheat plant and one cut moong plant, four days after the Cutting Test. Mark with a dot where each plant grows from.
items.answer_should_show: The wheat is taller, with flat leaf tips and a dot near the soil. The moong is a short stump, with the dot at the top of the stem, where the tip was cut off.

items.question: Draw a building with rainwater harvesting. Show the rain, the terrace, the pipe, the pit and the water going into the ground.
items.answer_should_show: Rain on the terrace, a pipe down the side, a pit of stones and sand, and arrows from the pit down into the ground.

items.question: Draw a grass leaf just after it is cut, and the same leaf three days later. Use an arrow to show where the new part grew.
items.answer_should_show: The second leaf is taller, with the same flat tip, and an arrow at the bottom near the soil showing new leaf added there.

items.question: Draw a bath with a tap and a drain. Label the tap 'births' and the drain 'catch'. Show the water as the number of fish in a pond.
items.answer_should_show: A bath with water in it, a tap labelled births running water in, and a drain labelled catch letting water out. The water level is labelled the fish in the pond.

items.question: Draw the tub model of groundwater at three stages: at the start, after pumping out one well, and after the rain. Mark the water level in each.
items.answer_should_show: At the start both holes have water at 3 centimetres. After pumping, the left hole is almost empty and the right hole is lower. After the rain, both holes are slightly higher but not as high as the start.

items.question: Draw a line graph over 20 years of the size of the biggest fish caught each year. Draw one line for a lake that is overfished, and another for a lake that is well looked after.
items.answer_should_show: The overfished line slopes steadily downwards over the 20 years. The well-looked-after line stays roughly level, with small ups and downs.

items.question: Draw your three sticky cards after three days: the flat one on the sill, the upright one on the grill, and the one from the dabba. Shade each square as grey as it was.
items.answer_should_show: The flat card darkest, the upright card lighter, the dabba card white.

items.question: Draw the path of one speck of soot from a bus exhaust to the inside of a child's nose. Show at least three places it passes.
items.answer_should_show: For example: out of the exhaust pipe, up into the air over the road, blown towards a building, in through an open window, into the nose with a breath, caught in the mucus.

items.question: Draw a food chain with plankton, a small fish, a big fish and a heron. Show a little pollution in the plankton, and draw how much builds up in each animal after that.
items.answer_should_show: Four animals in a row, with a few dots in the plankton and more and more dots in each one that comes after, ending with the most in the heron.

items.question: Draw a floating oil boom around a spill. Show the part above the water, the skirt under the water and the oil inside.
items.answer_should_show: A ring on the water with a float above the surface and a skirt hanging down below it, and oil inside the ring.

items.question: Draw a river from the hills to the sea. Mark one point source of pollution with a P and one place where runoff comes in with an R.
items.answer_should_show: A river drawn from the hills to the sea, with one pipe marked P from a factory or a town, and many thin streams marked R coming off fields or roads.

items.question: Draw yourself laughing, with the tissue flag in front of your mouth. Draw an arrow to show which way the air went.
items.answer_should_show: A laughing face with the flag blown away from the mouth, and an arrow pointing away from the mouth.

items.question: Draw an orangutan's nest high in a tree. Show the bent branches, and the soft leafy lining on top.
items.answer_should_show: A tree with a round platform of bent branches near the top, leaves on top, and an orangutan lying in it.

items.question: Design a sling for carrying a baby that leaves both hands free. Draw it on a person, and label where it ties.
items.answer_should_show: A drawing of a person with a cloth over one shoulder and round the body, the baby held against the back or chest, and a label at the knot.

items.question: Draw the clearest print and the blurriest print from your Print Test. Write under each one what made it.
items.answer_should_show: Two drawings, a sharp print of a hard thing and a blurry print of a soft thing, each labelled.

items.question: Draw an animal who is alive today. Draw a ring round the parts that would most likely become a fossil.
items.answer_should_show: A drawing of an animal with rings round the bones, teeth, shell, horns or claws.

items.question: Draw the peas from one of your pods in a row. Make each pea the size it really was.
items.answer_should_show: A row of peas of different sizes, all round.

items.question: Draw your thumb strip from the Practice Test. Show the 'before' mark and the 'after' mark where they really were.
items.answer_should_show: One strip with the two marks at the same place.

items.question: Draw two bean plants that grew from the same packet of seeds. One sat in the sun and one sat in a dark corner. Show how each plant looks after two weeks.
items.answer_should_show: One tall green plant in the sun, and one short pale or thin plant in the dark corner.

items.question: Draw the water bowl just after you added the water. Show where the bubbles were.
items.answer_should_show: A katori with powder and water, and bubbles rising all over it.

items.question: Draw a stromatolite cut in half, with its layers. Draw the mat of tiny cells on top, in the shallow sea.
items.answer_should_show: A dome of wavy layers, with a thin living layer on top and water above it.

items.question: Draw what you think the very first living cell looked like, floating in water. Label its thin skin and its watery inside.
items.answer_should_show: A tiny round cell with a thin skin and a watery inside, floating in water.

items.question: Draw a stromatolite cut open, and show its layers.
items.answer_should_show: A dome of rock with many thin wavy layers, one on top of the other.

items.question: Draw an experiment that could test whether building blocks of life can form without anything living. Show what you put in, where the energy comes from, and what you look for at the end.
items.answer_should_show: For example: a sealed flask with water and simple gases, sparks for energy, and a check for new chemicals, like amino acids, at the end.

items.question: Draw what you think the first cell looked like: a skin, and something inside that could be copied.
items.answer_should_show: A round bubble with a thin skin and a short chain of letters inside.

items.question: Draw three things in your home that you can know by their smell alone. Ask a grown-up to write what they are.
items.answer_should_show: A drawing of three things with a smell, such as tea, soap or a flower.

items.question: Microbes are too small to see. Draw what you think the microbes on your hand might look like, if you could zoom in.
items.answer_should_show: Any drawing of many tiny beings on a hand.

items.question: Draw how you would test if a grown-up at home can find YOUR shirt by smell. Show what makes it fair.
items.answer_should_show: A drawing of a grown-up with covered eyes, sniffing tumblers, with the child's shirt in one of them.

items.question: Draw an animal family you have seen near your home, like cats, crows or cows. Show who looks after the young.
items.answer_should_show: A drawing of an adult animal with her young.

items.question: Draw your family tree with three generations: grandparents at the top, parents in the middle, and you at the bottom. Write what you call each person.
items.answer_should_show: A tree with grandparents at the top, parents in the middle and the child at the bottom, with relation words.

items.question: Draw a balanced thali. Show the half for vegetables and fruit, and the two quarters.
items.answer_should_show: A plate with half vegetables and fruit, a quarter grains, a quarter protein foods like dal or curd, and a glass of water.

items.question: Draw the journey of a chapati from your mouth to a brain cell, in four boxes.
items.answer_should_show: Mouth (chewing and spit), stomach and small intestine (cut into glucose), blood (carrying glucose), brain cell (burning glucose for energy).

items.question: Draw yourself as a crowd: your own cells and your gut microbes. Show what each one gets from your lunch.
items.answer_should_show: Any drawing that shows cells getting glucose, amino acids and minerals, and microbes getting fibre and giving back food for gut cells.

items.question: Draw a plate for a festival meal that has all three food jobs. Label each food with its job.
items.answer_should_show: A plate with at least one energy food such as rice or roti, one body-building food such as dal or curd, and one protective food such as a vegetable or fruit, each labelled.

items.question: Draw a bowl of Ugadi pachadi with its six ingredients. Label the taste of each one.
items.answer_should_show: A bowl with six labelled ingredients: jaggery (sweet), tamarind (sour), salt (salty), neem flowers (bitter), pepper (pungent) and raw mango (astringent).

items.question: Draw three moong seeds in a row: a dry one, a soaked one and a sprouted one. Label what is different about each.
items.answer_should_show: A small hard seed labelled dry, a larger swollen seed labelled soaked, and a swollen seed with a small white tail labelled sprouted.

items.question: Draw dabba A and dabba C from the Three Dabbas test, as if you could see the microbes inside. Show which had more.
items.answer_should_show: Dabba A with only a few microbes, dabba C with many, crowded round the leaf.

items.question: Draw a thermometer from 0 to 100 degrees Celsius. Colour the band where microbes grow fastest, and mark where a fridge and boiling water are.
items.answer_should_show: A thermometer with the danger band from about 5 to 60 degrees coloured, the fridge below 5, and boiling at 100.

items.question: Draw a comic strip of 4 pictures showing a microbe's journey from a dustbin to a plate of food, and one habit that could stop them at each step.
items.answer_should_show: Four pictures, for example dustbin, fly, uncovered plate, mouth, with a stop such as a closed bin lid, a food cover, or washing hands.

items.question: Draw the table you would use to find which food made guests ill at a party. Show four foods and four columns, and circle how you would spot the suspect.
items.answer_should_show: A table with a row for each of four foods and four columns: ate and ill, ate and well, did not eat and ill, did not eat and well. The suspect row is circled where most eaters were ill and few non-eaters were.

items.question: Draw a cucumber slice and a tiny microbe, each in very salty water. Draw arrows to show which way the water moves.
items.answer_should_show: Arrows point from the cucumber slice, and from the inside of the microbe, out towards the salty water around them. The slice looks limp, and the microbe looks shrunken.

items.question: Draw a line graph of how much foam yeast might make over two hours in three places: a fridge, a counter and a warm bath. Draw one line for each place.
items.answer_should_show: The warm bath line rises fastest. The counter line rises more slowly. The fridge line stays almost flat.

items.question: Draw the squeeze test. Draw the hanky, the glass, and what dripped out.
items.answer_should_show: A twisted hanky over a glass, with drops falling from it.

items.question: Draw one thing you ate or drank today that had water in it.
items.answer_should_show: Any food or drink with water, such as a cucumber, fruit, curd, buttermilk or rice.

items.question: Draw where the water in a cucumber came from, before the plant drank the water.
items.answer_should_show: Rain falling on the ground, soaking into the soil, and going up the roots of the cucumber plant.

items.question: Draw a thali with one grow food, one go food, one protect food and one small treat. Label each one.
items.answer_should_show: Any thali with a food for each job and one small treat, labelled.

items.question: Draw a plate of food you like. Next to each food, write the nutrient it gives most.
items.answer_should_show: Any plate with each food labelled correctly. For example: rice, carbohydrate. Sambar, protein and water. Poriyal, vitamins and fibre. Curd, protein and calcium.

items.question: Draw two tumblers of milk: one before lemon juice is added, one 3 minutes after. Label what you see in each.
items.answer_should_show: Before: smooth white milk. After: white lumps (curds) in a thin pale yellow-green liquid (whey).

items.question: Draw a cycle that shows how the water in a cucumber could end up inside you, and then back in the air.
items.answer_should_show: Rain falls on soil, the cucumber plant drinks the water, you eat the cucumber, the water goes into your blood, and you breathe or sweat it back into the air, where it forms clouds.

items.question: Draw a plate of your own lunch. Colour each food by its main job and put a star by any food that does more than one job.
items.answer_should_show: A plate with several foods, each coloured for energy, building or protection, and stars by foods such as dal, curd or milk.

items.question: Draw how the energy gets from the Sun to a child. Label the Sun, a leaf, a groundnut, the child and an arrow for the heat leaving the child.
items.answer_should_show: A chain of drawings: the Sun, a leaf, a groundnut, a child eating, and an arrow of heat leaving the child's body.

items.question: Draw a bar chart for these foods in 100 grams: ghee 900 kilocalories, groundnuts 580, raw rice 350, cooked rice 130, cucumber 15. Choose a scale and label each bar.
items.answer_should_show: Five bars in order, with a scale where each centimetre stands for about 100 kilocalories, so ghee is about 9 centimetres tall, groundnuts about 6, raw rice about 3.5, cooked rice about 1.3 and cucumber almost nothing.

items.question: Draw your two plates from the sugar water test, the morning after. Show which drop ran when you tilted the plate.
items.answer_should_show: The open drop thick and still. The covered drop running down the plate.

items.question: Draw one food from a plant and one food from an animal that you ate today.
items.answer_should_show: Any two true examples, such as a dosa and a glass of milk.

items.question: In the Be a Bee challenge, which tool carried the most sugar water? Draw that tool and its bottle cap.
items.answer_should_show: A drawing of the best tool and a full cap.

items.question: Draw a soaked chana seed split open. Label the baby plant and the food store.
items.answer_should_show: A split seed with a small curled baby plant at one edge, and the two big halves labelled 'food store'.

items.question: Draw a whole plant and label six parts: root, stem, leaf, flower, fruit, seed. Next to each label, write a food from your own kitchen that is that part. Try not to use radish, sugarcane, methi, vazhaipoo, guava or moong.
items.answer_should_show: Root under the soil, for example carrot or beetroot. Stem, for example potato, an underground stem. Leaves, for example curry leaves or keerai. A flower, for example cauliflower. A fruit, for example tomato or brinjal. Seeds, for example rice or peanut.

items.question: Draw the Tap Test: the ball, the rolled newspaper, and you tapping it from the front.
items.answer_should_show: A ball, a newspaper tapper in front of it, and the child kneeling.

items.question: Draw something in your home that starts and stops many times a day. Draw an arrow for the push that starts it.
items.answer_should_show: Any thing that starts and stops, such as a door, a mixie, a fan or a person, with an arrow.

items.question: Draw a rowing boat stopping at the steps. Draw the oar pushing the water forward.
items.answer_should_show: A boat, a rower, and an oar pushing towards the front of the boat.

items.question: Draw the Bend Wall from above. Draw the marble's path with an arrow, from the start mark to after the wall ends.
items.answer_should_show: A curved wall, a curved arrow following the inside of the wall, and then a straight arrow leaving the end of the wall.

items.question: A ball is rolled at a slant towards a wall. Draw where it goes after it bounces.
items.answer_should_show: An arrow going to the wall at a slant, and an arrow coming away from the wall at a slant the other way.

items.question: Design a marble track that makes a marble turn two corners. Draw the walls and the marble's path.
items.answer_should_show: Two curved or slanted walls, with the path bending at each wall and going straight between them.

items.question: Draw a tennis ball at the moment it hits a cricket bat. Show how the ball's shape changes. Draw an arrow for the bat's push on the ball.
items.answer_should_show: A strong drawing shows the ball flattened on the side touching the bat. The arrow starts at the bat and points into the ball, back the way the ball came. The best drawings say the ball will then spring back and fly off the other way.

items.question: Design a sandal sole that can bend when you walk but never snaps. Label which parts squash and which parts stretch when it bends.
items.answer_should_show: Any thoughtful design. The top of the bend is squashed and the bottom is stretched, or the other way round when it bends the other way. Soft rubber, or grooves across the sole, help it bend.

items.question: Draw how the Himalayas were made. First draw India's plate moving north towards Asia, with an arrow for the push. Then draw the rock between them after the push, folded up into mountains.
items.answer_should_show: A strong drawing shows two blocks of land with flat layers of rock between them, and an arrow pushing one block towards the other. The second picture shows the layers crumpled and folded upwards, like a towel pushed against a wall.

items.question: Draw a bamboo scaffold pole bending in a strong wind. Mark the side that is squashed and the side that is stretched. Draw an arrow for the wind's push.
items.answer_should_show: A strong drawing shows the pole curved away from the wind. The arrow points at the pole from the windward side. The inside of the curve is marked squashed and the outside is marked stretched.

items.question: Draw a paper plane flying. Draw four arrows on it: lift, weight, thrust and drag. Label each.
items.answer_should_show: Lift points up, weight points down, thrust points forward and drag points back.

items.question: A plane turns by tipping one wing down. Draw a plane from the front, tipped to its right. Draw the lift arrow at right angles to the wings. Which way will the plane turn?
items.answer_should_show: A strong drawing shows the wings sloping down to the right, with the lift arrow leaning to the right too. The plane turns right, because part of the lift now pulls it sideways. A cheel turning in a thermal tips their wings in just the same way.

items.question: Invent a new seed that flies. Draw it. Label the part that pushes on the air, and where the heavy seed sits. Say how the shape of your seed slows the fall.
items.answer_should_show: A strong design has a wide wing, a parachute or fluff that pushes on lots of air, with the heavy seed low down or at one end, so the seed falls steadily instead of tumbling. It says how the shape slows the fall, so the wind can carry the seed far.

items.question: Draw a parachute falling at a steady speed. Draw an arrow for its weight and an arrow for the drag, and say how long each arrow is.
items.answer_should_show: A parachute with a down arrow for weight and an up arrow for drag. Both arrows are the same length.

items.question: Draw a V of geese seen from above. Add small arrows to show where the air rises beside the wing tip of the goose in front.
items.answer_should_show: A V shape with a goose at the front and others behind, each slightly to one side. Small upward arrows are drawn just outside the wing tip of each goose.

items.question: Draw a card swished through smoke. Show the smoke before the swish, and the whirls after the card has stopped.
items.answer_should_show: A thin straight line of smoke, then a second drawing with the line bent into curls and spirals beside the card, which is held still.

items.question: Draw your two hands rubbing together, the right hand moving up and the left hand moving down. Draw an arrow for the friction on each hand.
items.answer_should_show: On the right hand, the friction arrow points down. On the left hand, it points up. Each arrow points against the way that hand is moving.

items.question: Design a shoe sole for walking on the wet, mossy steps of a ghat. Label two features that give more grip.
items.answer_should_show: Good features include soft rubber, deep grooves to let water out, small bumps or studs, and a wide flat area that touches the stone.

items.question: Draw a close-up of two 'smooth' surfaces touching, as a very strong microscope would show them. Mark the places where they really touch.
items.answer_should_show: Two bumpy edges, like mountain ranges, touching only at a few peaks. The touching peaks are marked.

items.question: Draw two rough surfaces pressed together, and show where they really touch. Then draw them pressed together harder.
items.answer_should_show: Two mountain-range surfaces touching at a few peaks. In the second drawing, the peaks are flattened and more peaks touch.

items.question: Draw a rope wound twice round a post. Draw a big arrow for the boat's pull and a very small arrow for the hold on the loose end.
items.answer_should_show: A post with two loops of rope, a long arrow on the boat side and a short arrow on the loose end.

items.question: Draw a line graph of these made-up results. Loads: 0, 1, 2, 3 and 4 packets. Stretches: 0, 2, 4, 6 and 8 centimetres.
items.answer_should_show: Packets along the bottom and stretch up the side, with dots at (0,0), (1,2), (2,4), (3,6), (4,8) joined in a straight line.

items.question: Draw a toy that rolls. Colour the round parts that touch the ground.
items.answer_should_show: A toy with round parts touching the ground, such as a car with wheels or a ball.

items.question: Draw the path a bottle makes when it rolls on the floor. Then draw the path a paper cup makes.
items.answer_should_show: A straight line for the bottle and a curved line, part of a circle, for the cup.

items.question: Draw a forcemeter. Label the hook, the spring, the pointer and the scale. Then draw the pointer where it would be for a pull of 2 newtons.
items.answer_should_show: A tube with a spring inside and a hook at the bottom. A pointer is fixed to the spring, next to a scale numbered 0, 1, 2, 3 and so on. The pointer is drawn level with the 2.

items.question: Draw your rubber band forcemeter with two marks on its card: 0 newtons and 1 newton. Draw what you hung on it to find where the 1 newton mark goes.
items.answer_should_show: A rubber band hanging from the top of a card strip, with a paper clip hook at the bottom. A 0 mark is level with the hook when nothing hangs on it. A 1 newton mark is lower down, level with the hook when a 100 gram packet hangs on it.

items.question: Design a forcemeter that could show the pull of a single sheet of paper. Draw it and label how it works.
items.answer_should_show: For example, a long plastic ruler taped to the edge of a table, sticking out. The paper hangs from the far end, and a straw taped on as a pointer shows the bend against marks on a card.

items.question: Draw a book lying on a table. Use arrows to show its weight of 8 N and the push of the table. Use 1 cm for each 1 N. Label each arrow.
items.answer_should_show: A book with an arrow 8 cm long pointing down, labelled 'weight 8 N', and an arrow 8 cm long pointing up, labelled 'push of the table 8 N'.

items.question: Three forces act on a box: 6 N right, 4 N right and 3 N left. Draw all three with 1 cm for each 1 N. Then draw the net force.
items.answer_should_show: Three arrows on a box: 6 cm and 4 cm pointing right, and 3 cm pointing left. The net force is an arrow 7 cm long, pointing right.

items.question: Draw a bottle hanging in the middle of a sagging line. Show the weight and the pulls of the two sides. Make the side arrows longer than the weight arrow and say why.
items.answer_should_show: A bottle with a short arrow pointing down labelled weight, and two longer arrows along the line pointing up and outwards. A note says that only the upward part of each side's pull holds the bottle, so each side pulls more than half the weight.

items.question: Draw yourself pushing something. Show it moving away from you.
items.answer_should_show: A child pushing a thing, such as a swing or a ball, with the thing moving away.

items.question: Draw yourself pulling something. Show it coming towards you.
items.answer_should_show: A child pulling a thing, such as a drawer or a toy on a string, with the thing coming closer.

items.question: Draw a machine you have seen, such as a tractor, a crane or a bulldozer. Show if it pushes or pulls, and which way the thing moves.
items.answer_should_show: Any machine drawn with the thing it moves, and an arrow showing the push or the pull.

items.question: Draw one force in your home. Draw who or what gives the force, and the thing it moves.
items.answer_should_show: Any real push or pull, with the giver and the thing moved, such as a hand opening a door or a fan blowing a paper.

items.question: Draw yourself holding a heavy bag. Show where you feel the pull.
items.answer_should_show: A child holding a bag, with the fingers or shoulder marked where the pull is felt.

items.question: Draw a way to show the secret packet going into a heavy bag, without using your hand to feel it.
items.answer_should_show: A balance, a hanger with two bags, a rubber band that stretches more, or a scale.

items.question: Draw a girl pulling a toy cart along with a string. Draw an arrow for the pull on the cart. Make the arrow start on the cart.
items.answer_should_show: An arrow starting on the cart and pointing along the string, towards the girl.

items.question: Draw a girl pushing a swing. Draw an arrow for her push on the swing. Then draw an arrow for the swing's push back on her.
items.answer_should_show: One arrow starts on the swing and points away from the girl. A second arrow, the same length, starts on the girl and points back towards her.

items.question: Draw yourself standing on the Earth. Draw an arrow for the Earth pulling you, and an arrow for you pulling the Earth. How long should each arrow be?
items.answer_should_show: One arrow starts on the child and points down towards the Earth. An equal arrow starts on the Earth and points up towards the child.

items.question: Draw a see-saw with a grown-up and a child sitting on it, balanced and level. Mark the fulcrum. Show who sits closer to it.
items.answer_should_show: The grown-up sits close to the middle. The child sits near the far end. The fulcrum is the post in the middle, marked with a triangle.

items.question: Design a ramp for a toy car to reach a 10 cm high box. Draw a short steep ramp and a long gentle ramp. Mark which needs the smaller push.
items.answer_should_show: Two ramps from the floor to the top of the box. The long gentle ramp is marked as the smaller push.

items.question: Draw your own design for a machine that lifts a bucket of water from a well, using at least two simple machines. Label each one.
items.answer_should_show: Any design using two or more simple machines, labelled. For example: a lever like a shaduf with a stone counterweight, and a pulley wheel.

items.question: Draw a bottle hanging from a moving pulley with 2 ropes. Draw an arrow on each rope. If the bottle weighs 10 newtons, write the pull in each rope.
items.answer_should_show: A bottle hanging from a wheel in a loop of rope, with two upward arrows on the two ropes, each labelled 5 newtons.

items.question: Draw a block and tackle with 3 ropes holding a load of 30 newtons. Write the pull in each rope and how far your hand moves for a 1 metre lift.
items.answer_should_show: A load hanging from a moving block with 3 ropes going up to a fixed block, each rope labelled 10 newtons, and a note that the hand moves 3 metres.

items.question: Draw a rubber band between two fingers: first loose, then stretched. On the stretched band, draw arrows to show how it pulls on your fingers.
items.answer_should_show: two pictures. Loose band: a small loop. Stretched band: a long loop, with arrows pointing inwards from both ends.

items.question: Draw a simple catapult made from a bent stick or rubber bands, pressed down and ready to fire. Label where the energy is stored before you let go.
items.answer_should_show: A drawing of the catapult with the arm pressed down. The label points to the bent stick or the stretched rubber bands.

items.question: Draw a model of the atoms in a spring, as balls joined by tiny springs. Then draw it again when the spring is stretched.
items.answer_should_show: Two drawings. In the first, the balls are evenly spaced with short springs between them. In the second, the balls are a little further apart and every tiny spring is a little longer.

items.question: Draw a graph with the pull along the bottom and the stretch up the side. Draw one line for a stiff spring and one for a soft spring. Label each line.
items.answer_should_show: Two straight lines from the corner. The soft spring's line climbs steeply upward, since it stretches a lot for each newton. The stiff spring's line climbs gently, since it stretches only a little for each newton.

items.question: Draw two bands in a row and two bands side by side, each holding the same packet. If one band stretches 10 cm, write how far each group stretches.
items.answer_should_show: Two bands in a row, hanging in a chain with the packet at the bottom, labelled 20 cm. Two bands side by side, both holding the packet, labelled 5 cm.

items.question: Draw a graph showing how big the bag's bounce is, as the speed of the shaking hand goes from slow to fast. Mark where the bag's natural beat is.
items.answer_should_show: A hill-shaped curve: low for slow shaking, rising to a peak at the natural beat, and falling again for fast shaking. The peak is marked as the natural beat.

items.question: Draw the seed leaves of a mustard seedling and a methi seedling, side by side. Label each one.
items.answer_should_show: Mustard: two tiny heart-shaped leaves, each with a notch at the top. Methi: two small, smooth, oval leaves.

items.question: Draw a cell as a big circle with a nucleus inside. Draw the DNA in the nucleus, an RNA copy leaving it, and a ribosome building a protein. Label all four.
items.answer_should_show: A big circle with a smaller circle inside. In the small circle, a long twisted line labelled DNA. A short line labelled RNA crossing out of the nucleus. A small round ribosome with a chain of beads, labelled protein.

items.question: Draw a twisted ladder of DNA with 6 rungs. Write a letter on each end of every rung. Remember: A always pairs with T, and C with G.
items.answer_should_show: Six rungs, each with one of the pairs A and T, T and A, C and G, or G and C. For example A-T, C-G, G-C, T-A, A-T, G-C.

items.question: Draw one thing you let go of in the Let-Go Test. Draw an arrow to show which way it went.
items.answer_should_show: Any thing from the test, with an arrow pointing down.

items.question: Draw yourself jumping. Then draw yourself landing. Draw an arrow to show the Earth's pull.
items.answer_should_show: Two pictures: the child in the air, then on the ground, with an arrow pointing down.

items.question: Draw the dot on the newspaper. Draw the lemon falling onto it. Then draw the path a sheet of paper took as it fell.
items.answer_should_show: A straight line down onto the dot for the lemon, and a wobbly, swinging line for the paper, landing away from the dot.

items.question: Draw Galileo's Ramp with the marble's place after beats 1, 2, 3 and 4. Show how the gaps between the marks change.
items.answer_should_show: A sloping ramp with four marks. The gap from the start to the first mark is small, and each gap after that is bigger than the one before.

items.question: Draw a skydiver falling at her top speed. Draw one arrow for her weight and one arrow for the push of the air. Make the arrows the right lengths.
items.answer_should_show: A skydiver with a downward arrow for weight and an upward arrow for the push of the air, both the same length.

items.question: Draw the path of a ball rolled off a table and the path of a ball dropped from the table's edge. Show where each is after each tenth of a second.
items.answer_should_show: Two dotted paths starting at the table's edge. The dropped ball goes straight down. The rolled ball curves out. At each tenth of a second, both are at the same height.

items.question: Draw dots to show where a ball thrown sideways is after each tenth of a second. Show that it moves the same distance sideways each time, and farther down each time.
items.answer_should_show: A row of dots in a curve. The dots are the same distance apart across the page and the gaps between them go down more and more.

items.question: Draw yourself standing on the floor. Draw one arrow for gravity's pull on you and one arrow for the floor's push on you.
items.answer_should_show: The gravity arrow points down from the middle of the body. The floor's arrow points up from the feet. The two arrows are the same length.

items.question: Draw yourself standing in a lift that is just starting to go up. Draw one arrow for gravity's pull on you and one arrow for the floor's push on you. Make the bigger force the longer arrow.
items.answer_should_show: The gravity arrow points down. The floor's arrow points up from the feet, and it is a little longer than the gravity arrow.

items.question: Draw the space station going round the Earth. Draw an arrow for gravity's pull on it, and an arrow for the way it is moving.
items.answer_should_show: The gravity arrow points from the station to the centre of the Earth. The movement arrow points sideways, along the circle.

items.question: Draw a cardboard ring hanging from a pin. Draw a plumb line down from the pin, and mark where the centre of gravity is.
items.answer_should_show: The ring hangs from the pin at its top. The plumb line is a straight vertical line down from the pin, through the empty hole. The centre of gravity is a dot on that line in the middle of the hole.

items.question: Draw a bucket tilted halfway over on the floor. Draw the line straight down from its centre of gravity, and show whether it will tip back or fall over.
items.answer_should_show: The bucket is tilted on one bottom edge. The vertical line from the centre of gravity falls inside that edge, so the bucket tips back. If the line fell outside the edge, it would fall over.

items.question: Draw the Earth and the Moon, and mark the point they both circle. Show where that point is.
items.answer_should_show: The Earth is a big circle, and the Moon is a small circle far to one side. A dot is marked on the line between them, inside the Earth's circle, nearer the Earth's edge than its centre.

items.question: Draw your bottle fish twice: once with no air, and once with a little air. Show where each one was in the bucket.
items.answer_should_show: One bottle on the bottom of the bucket, and one at the top with a small air space inside.

items.question: Draw a plant for a very dry place. Give your plant one adaptation that saves water, and say what it does.
items.answer_should_show: A plant with thick leaves, spines, a waxy skin or very small leaves, with a sentence about how it saves water.

items.question: Draw how you made your bottle fish hang in the middle of the water, or how you would try. Label the air and the coins.
items.answer_should_show: A bottle in the middle of a bucket, with a small air space at the top and coins at the bottom.

items.question: Draw a duck's foot under water. Show the skin between their toes.
items.answer_should_show: A foot with three front toes joined by skin, spread out like a paddle.

items.question: Draw a fat cactus and a big thin leaf. Draw arrows to show where water escapes from each. Which has more arrows?
items.answer_should_show: The thin leaf has arrows all over its big surface. The cactus has fewer arrows for their size.

items.question: Design a plant for the Thar Desert. Label three features and the problem each one solves.
items.answer_should_show: For example: a fat stem to store water, a waxy coat to stop water escaping, and very deep roots to reach water underground.

items.question: Draw yourself in round 2 of the noise test. Show the noise next to you and the soft words going towards you.
items.answer_should_show: A drawing of the child facing the wall, the noise maker close by, and only a few words reaching them.

items.question: A new glass building has no holes or ledges. Draw one change that would give sparrows a place to nest.
items.answer_should_show: A nest box on the wall, a gap under the roof, or a small ledge with a hole, high up and out of reach of cats.

items.question: Draw your diya and your stone in the plate of water. Draw the seeds on each top as they looked on day 3.
items.answer_should_show: The diya has sprouted seeds with little roots or green leaves. The stone has dry seeds that did not grow.

items.question: Draw a rock with three living beings on it, under it or in its cracks.
items.answer_should_show: For example: moss on top, a lizard in a crack and ants underneath.

items.question: Draw a pond cut in half, so we can see inside. Show one living thing at the top of the water, one in the middle and one in the mud at the bottom.
items.answer_should_show: For example: a lotus leaf or a water strider at the top, a fish in the middle, a snail or a worm in the mud. A strong drawing also shows where the light is brightest.

items.question: Draw the soil from your plate test. Colour the wet soil dark brown and the dry soil pale.
items.answer_should_show: The half that was under the plate is coloured dark. The half in the sun is pale.

items.question: Draw a tree. Draw three different homes on your tree: one high up, one on the bark and one near the roots.
items.answer_should_show: For example, a crow's nest high up, ants on the bark, and an earthworm or a pill bug in the soil at the roots.

items.question: Draw a pond. Show a lotus, a frog, a fish and some algae, each in the part of the pond where they live.
items.answer_should_show: Lotus leaves above the water with roots in the mud, a frog at the edge, a fish in the water and algae near the top, where the light is.

items.question: Draw a line graph of the oxygen in a green pond from noon one day to noon the next day. Mark where it is highest and where it is lowest.
items.answer_should_show: The line rises through the afternoon while the algae make oxygen, falls through the evening and all night, is lowest just before sunrise, then rises again after sunrise.

items.question: Draw a fish and show with arrows how water goes in and out as they breathe.
items.answer_should_show: An arrow into the mouth, over the gills, and out under the gill cover.

items.question: Draw yourself right after the fast dance. Show what your face and chest looked like.
items.answer_should_show: A child with a red face, open mouth, and lines to show fast breathing.

items.question: Draw three towers of blocks: your breaths sitting still, right after dancing, and after 2 minutes of rest.
items.answer_should_show: Three towers: a short one, a tall one, and a middle one.

items.question: Draw the path of one breath of oxygen: from a plant, into your nose, to your lungs, to your leg muscle.
items.answer_should_show: A drawing with arrows from a plant, to the nose, to the lungs, to the heart and blood, to the leg.

items.question: Draw yourself in tree pose. Mark the leg muscles that are working hardest.
items.answer_should_show: A child standing on one leg, with the standing leg's calf, thigh and ankle marked.

items.question: Draw a bar chart of these made-up peg counts: round 1, 50. Round 2, 42. Round 3, 37. Round 4, 33. Round 5 after a two-minute rest, 46.
items.answer_should_show: Five bars, falling from 50 to 33, then a tall bar of 46 for the round after rest.

items.question: Draw a 24-hour circle for a healthy day for a child of 8. Show sleep, school or study, play and exercise, and meals.
items.answer_should_show: A circle of 24 slices with 9 to 10 slices for sleep, about 6 for school or study, at least 1 for active play, and slices for meals.

items.question: Draw your face when you feel happy. Then draw your face when you feel cross.
items.answer_should_show: Two faces: one smiling, one with eyebrows down or a frown.

items.question: Draw a helper that would work for you when you feel scared at night.
items.answer_should_show: For example: a night light, a hug, a soft toy, slow breaths.

items.question: Draw two faces: a scared face and a surprised face. Show the difference in the eyebrows and mouth.
items.answer_should_show: Both have raised eyebrows and wide eyes. The scared face has eyebrows pulled together and lips stretched back. The surprised face has a rounded, open mouth.

items.question: Draw your calm corner plan. Label three things in it and say how each one helps.
items.answer_should_show: Any plan that fits in a small space, with three labelled things, such as a cushion for comfort, a calm bottle to watch, and a picture card for slow breathing.

items.question: Draw a comic of four boxes. In it, someone guesses a friend's feeling wrong from their face, then finds out by asking.
items.answer_should_show: Four boxes: a face, a wrong guess, a question, and the real feeling.

items.question: Remember the biscuit test? Draw a back tooth. Draw where the crumbs stayed after you swished water.
items.answer_should_show: A wide tooth with grooves on top, and crumbs drawn inside the grooves.

items.question: Draw yourself having a bath. Draw what the water is washing off you.
items.answer_should_show: A child pouring water or under a shower, with dust, sweat drops or tiny flakes washing off.

items.question: Draw your mouth as a home. Who lives there? What do they eat?
items.answer_should_show: A mouth with teeth, and tiny beings drawn on and between the teeth, with crumbs of food near them.

items.question: Draw a soap molecule. Label the head that sticks to water and the tail that sticks to oil.
items.answer_should_show: A round head labelled 'sticks to water' and a long tail labelled 'sticks to oil'.

items.question: Draw a micelle: a ring of soap molecules around a blob of oil. Show which way the heads and tails point.
items.answer_should_show: A ring of soap molecules with their tails pointing into an oil blob in the middle, and their heads pointing out into the water.

items.question: Draw your two rows of eight boxes from the picture-pairs test. Colour a box for each pair you remembered later.
items.answer_should_show: Two rows, with the night-set row usually having as many or more coloured boxes.

items.question: Some plants fold their leaves at night. Draw a tamarind or touch-me-not branch in the day, and the same branch at night.
items.answer_should_show: The day branch has leaves spread open. The night branch has the leaves folded together.

items.question: Draw something at home that you wonder about. Then say your question out loud, and a grown-up writes it.
items.answer_should_show: A drawing of one thing, and a question about it that starts with what, why or how.

items.question: Draw an animal finding out about something new. Show the body part they use.
items.answer_should_show: For example: an ant touching a crumb with her feelers, a dog sniffing, or a crow looking with one eye.

items.question: Draw the Rice Bottle Lift. Show the bottle, the rice and the pencil when the bottle lifted.
items.answer_should_show: A drawing of a bottle full of rice hanging from a pencil held by a hand.

items.question: Draw something you could test at home. Then say your test question, and a grown-up writes it.
items.answer_should_show: A drawing of something to test, with a question like 'Does a lemon float?'

items.question: Draw the rice grains in loose rice and in packed rice, around a pencil. Show where the gaps are.
items.answer_should_show: Loose rice drawn with spaces between grains. Packed rice drawn with grains touching each other and the pencil.

items.question: Draw the three apple slices from the brown apple watch as they looked after one hour: plain, lemon and under water. Colour them and write each one's score.
items.answer_should_show: The plain slice brown or light brown (score 2 or 3), the lemon slice still cream (score 0), and the water slice pale or a little yellow (score 0 or 1).

items.question: Draw a plan card for the banana diary. Show your question, how often you will look, what you will count, and how you will record it.
items.answer_should_show: A card with a question (for example 'How fast does the banana get brown spots?'), 'every morning at 8', 'count spots and score the colour', and a small table or photo plan.

items.question: Draw two columns headed 'I saw' and 'I think'. Write three sentences about a crow on your railing in the correct columns.
items.answer_should_show: A page with two columns. Under 'I saw': for example, 'A crow sits on the railing' and 'The crow turns their head'. Under 'I think': for example, 'The crow is hungry'.

items.question: Eight people had these differences between arm span and height, in centimetres: 0, +2, −1, +3, −4, +1, 0, +12. Draw a number line from −5 to +15 and put a dot for each person. Circle the one that does not fit.
items.answer_should_show: A number line from −5 to +15 with seven dots near zero and one dot at +12, circled.

items.question: Draw a model of the mist that appears on a bathroom mirror after a hot shower. Show the air, the water vapour, the mirror and where the drops come from.
items.answer_should_show: A mirror with warm moist air near it, dots of vapour, and tiny drops forming on the cooler glass.

items.question: Draw a results table for the Brown Apple Test. Give it headings for what you put on each slice and the colour at 10 and 30 minutes. Fill in your own results.
items.answer_should_show: A table with 4 rows (nothing, water, salt water, lemon) and columns with clear headings, filled in with the child's own scores.

items.question: Draw a results table for Ten Throws, with rows for underarm and overarm and columns for the tally and the number in.
items.answer_should_show: A table with two rows and three columns: Throw, Tally, Number in out of 10.

items.question: Draw a bar chart of these Ten Throws results: underarm 7, overarm 4. Label both bars and the side of the chart.
items.answer_should_show: Two bars, underarm up to 7 and overarm up to 4, with a side scale from 0 to 10 labelled 'Balls in'.

items.question: Draw a results table for testing three straw widths, with five drops each. Give it headings for the straw width, each try, the average and the range.
items.answer_should_show: A table with a row for each of three straw widths. Columns headed Width (mm), Try 1 to Try 5 (ml), Average (ml) and Range (ml).

items.question: A spinner with 4 centimetre wings took an average of 12 tenths of a second, one with 6 centimetre wings took 16, and one with 8 centimetre wings took 21. Draw a line graph of these averages, with labelled axes.
items.answer_should_show: A graph with wing length (cm) along the bottom and average time (tenths of a second) up the side, with dots at (4, 12), (6, 16), (8, 21) joined by straight lines.

items.question: Four bridge shapes held on average 1, 8, 15 and 17 coins. Draw a bar chart with the shapes flat, channel, pleated and tube, and label the axes.
items.answer_should_show: A bar chart with four bars of heights 1, 8, 15 and 17, labelled flat, channel, pleated and tube, with the vertical axis labelled coins held.

items.question: A jar has a layer of chana on top and a layer of moong at the bottom. Draw the jar. Show a spoonful taken from the top, and label the part the spoonful misses.
items.answer_should_show: A jar with two layers, a spoon at the top in the chana, and a label on the moong at the bottom saying 'missed'.

items.question: Draw a tally chart with four boxes for the Crow and Guest Week: crow and guest, crow and no guest, no crow and guest, no crow and no guest. Fill it in with made-up numbers that would show the saying is wrong.
items.answer_should_show: Any numbers where guests come about as often on no-crow days as on crow days, for example 2 out of 5 crow days and 2 out of 5 no-crow days.

items.question: Draw a cartoon in three boxes showing how a true message could turn false as it is passed on. Show who first saw what happened.
items.answer_should_show: Three boxes: someone sees something and tells a friend, the friend passes it on with a change, and the last person tells a very different story.

items.question: Draw a diagram with three circles. Show a hidden third thing with an arrow to each of two things that go together. Use the beach, or your own example.
items.answer_should_show: A sun circle with arrows to a gola circle and a sunburn circle, and a dotted line with a cross between the gola and the sunburn.

items.question: A friend says playing music helps bean seeds sprout faster. Draw a fair test with two trays, a coin, and what stays the same.
items.answer_should_show: Two trays with the same beans, same water, same light and same warmth. A coin decides which seeds go to which tray. Only one tray has music.

items.question: Children who have more books at home do better at school. Draw a diagram with one or two hidden third things behind both.
items.answer_should_show: Circles for books at home and school marks, with arrows from a third circle such as parents who read, family money or time at home, to both.

items.question: Draw your haldi paper. Colour the boxes that went red.
items.answer_should_show: A yellow paper with red boxes for soap and cooking soda.

items.question: Draw the red spot after you added lemon juice in Back to Yellow.
items.answer_should_show: A yellow spot, or a pale orange one turning yellow.

items.question: Draw what you saw on the newspaper after you peeled off the fresh tape. Label any torn or furry part.
items.answer_should_show: A drawing of the newspaper with a grey, furry patch or a torn strip where the fresh tape was, labelled.

items.question: Design a fair credit page for the pulsar discovery. Include everyone you know about: who built the telescope, who noticed, who led, who explained.
items.answer_should_show: A page listing the jobs with names: Bell (built, noticed, checked), Hewish (led, designed), and others such as the team who helped build it and the scientists who explained pulsars as spinning dead stars.

items.question: Draw a side view of a drop of water in a hole in foil. Draw two lines of light going through the drop towards an eye.
items.answer_should_show: A drop with a curved top and bottom in the hole, and two lines of light that bend as they enter the drop and spread out towards an eye above.

items.question: Draw three pieces of string side by side, one centimetre for each year, for waits of 3 years, 50 years and 190 years. Label each.
items.answer_should_show: Three strings, one very short, one much longer, and one nearly two metres long, each labelled with its number of years.

items.question: Draw two panels. In the first, write a vague step for a job. In the second, write a clear step for the same job.
items.answer_should_show: Any job, such as 'Add water' against 'Pour one cup, 250 millilitres, of water into the steel pot'.

items.question: Draw three things on or near your street that were paid for with public money. Label each one.
items.answer_should_show: Any three shared things, such as a road, a street light and a bus stop, each labelled.

items.question: A job card is a worker's own record under the rural job guarantee. Draw a job card for a grandmother who dug a farm pond and worked 15 days in April. Show the days she worked and the wages she was paid.
items.answer_should_show: A drawing of a small booklet with her name, a table of dates or days, and a wage column.

items.question: Make a picture poster for families who cannot read. It should tell them that every child aged 6 to 14 has a free school place.
items.answer_should_show: A poster that a person who cannot read could understand: a child, a school, the numbers 6 and 14, and a sign that it costs nothing.

items.question: Draw two fist prints in damp atta: one from a gentle press and one from a hard press. Write how wide each was.
items.answer_should_show: Two prints, the hard one wider, with widths written below, for example 5 cm and 7 cm.

items.question: Draw how a camera trap is set up on a forest path, so that it photographs both sides of a tiger.
items.answer_should_show: A path with one camera on each side, both pointing at the path.

items.question: Design a symbol for your family, like the ₹ symbol joins two letters. Draw it, and write what each part stands for.
items.answer_should_show: Any clear, simple symbol with a short explanation for each part.

items.question: Draw a plate with red, yellow and blue paint. Show two of the paints mixing, and the new colour they make in the middle. Colour it in.
items.answer_should_show: A plate with red, yellow and blue blobs, and a green, orange or purple patch where two met.

items.question: Draw a green parrot. Then colour the two paints you would mix to paint them.
items.answer_should_show: A green parrot, with a yellow blob and a blue blob beside the parrot.

items.question: Draw a bee flying to a bright flower. Colour the flower.
items.answer_should_show: A bee near a brightly coloured flower.

items.question: Draw a torch shining on yellow paint and on brown paint. Draw more arrows of light coming back from the one that sends back more light.
items.answer_should_show: More arrows coming back from the yellow paint, and very few from the brown.

items.question: Draw yourself seeing a rainbow. Draw the Sun, the rain and the rainbow in the right places.
items.answer_should_show: The Sun is behind the person. The rain and the rainbow are in front of them. Red is on the outside of the bow. A strong drawing also shows the person's shadow pointing towards the rainbow.

items.question: Draw a prism with a white beam going in. Draw the colours coming out, in the right order. Show which colour bends most.
items.answer_should_show: A white beam enters one side. Colours fan out of the other side, with red bent least and violet bent most.

items.question: Draw a big raindrop with a ray of sunlight going in. Show the light bending as it enters, bouncing off the back of the drop, and bending again as it comes out. Show red and violet coming out at different angles.
items.answer_should_show: The ray enters the upper part of the drop and bends. It bounces off the back inside the drop. It comes out lower down, bending again, and spreads into colours. Red and violet leave at slightly different angles, so they go to different places.

items.question: Draw a red torch and a green torch shining on a white wall. Show where the wall looks red, where it looks green and where it looks yellow.
items.answer_should_show: The red torch lights one round patch red. The green torch lights another patch green. Where the two patches overlap, the wall looks yellow.

items.question: Draw a red, a green and a blue torch shining on one spot of a white wall. Label the colour in the middle. Label the colour where just two beams overlap.
items.answer_should_show: The three beams overlap in the middle, which looks white. Red and green overlap as yellow. Green and blue overlap as cyan. Red and blue overlap as magenta.

items.question: Draw a white wall lit by a red torch on the left and a blue torch on the right, with a pencil in front. Colour the lit wall and the two shadows.
items.answer_should_show: The middle where both lights reach looks magenta. The shadow where the red light is blocked looks blue. The shadow where the blue light is blocked looks red.

items.question: Draw a cat in a dark lane with glowing eyes, and a person holding a torch. Draw arrows to show where the glow comes from.
items.answer_should_show: An arrow from the torch to the cat's eye, and an arrow bouncing back from the cat's eye to the person.

items.question: Draw two eyes side by side. One is in bright sunshine and one is in a dim room. Draw the pupil in each, and label the pupil.
items.answer_should_show: The eye in sunshine has a small pupil. The eye in the dim room has a big pupil, with only a thin iris ring around it.

items.question: A scholar makes a small hole in the shutter of a dark room. A donkey stands outside in the sunlight. Draw the room, the hole and the donkey. Draw arrows to show how the picture of the donkey got onto the wall.
items.answer_should_show: An arrow from the Sun to the donkey, then arrows from the donkey, through the hole, to the wall.

items.question: Draw a ray diagram of a lamp, a mango and an eye. Use a ruler and draw straight arrows to show how you see the mango.
items.answer_should_show: One arrow goes from the lamp to the mango. Another arrow goes from the mango into the eye. Both arrows are straight and point the way the light travels.

items.question: Draw a candle, a lens and a white card. Show rays from the tip of the flame crossing at the lens and meeting on the card. Show how the picture on the card is upside down.
items.answer_should_show: Rays from the flame tip spread out, pass through the lens and cross, and meet at a point at the bottom of the card. The picture of the flame is upside down.

items.question: Draw a top-down picture of a head with two eyes looking at a pencil held in front, with a wall behind. Draw the line of sight from each eye to the pencil and on to the wall. Mark where the pencil seems to be on the wall for each eye.
items.answer_should_show: Two lines start at the two eyes and meet at the pencil. They carry on to the wall and land at two different places. The distance between the two places is the jump.

items.question: Draw three light sources you can find in your home. Draw rays coming out of each one.
items.answer_should_show: Three light sources, such as a tube light, a torch, a phone screen, a diya or the Sun through a window, each with rays.

items.question: In the dark room, you shine the torch on the steel spoon. Draw what you see. Draw the light going from the torch to the spoon.
items.answer_should_show: A torch with a beam, and a spoon shining where the beam lands. The rest is dark.

items.question: Draw the Sun, the Moon and your home at night. Draw arrows to show how the light gets to your window.
items.answer_should_show: An arrow from the Sun to the Moon, and an arrow from the Moon to the home.

items.question: Draw a shut box with a small hole in its side, and a piece of black paper next to it. Colour the hole and the black paper. Make the darker one darker.
items.answer_should_show: The hole is coloured darker than the black paper.

items.question: Draw a picture that shows darkness. Then write: how did you show it, when darkness is no light?
items.answer_should_show: Any honest drawing, for example a black shut cupboard, with a sentence like: I drew no light reaching inside.

items.question: Draw a firefly at night. Show where their light comes from. Draw an arrow for the air going in.
items.answer_should_show: A beetle with their glowing lantern at the end of their body, and an arrow of air going into the lantern.

items.question: Draw a glow stick before you bend it and after. Show what happens inside the tube.
items.answer_should_show: The first drawing shows a plain tube with a small glass tube inside. The second shows the glass tube cracked, two liquids mixing and light coming out.

items.question: Draw a deep-sea scene with three animals. Give each one a light with a different job: catch food, hide, scare an attacker or talk. Label the jobs.
items.answer_should_show: For example, an anglerfish with a lure (catch food), a hatchetfish with belly lights (hide), and a jellyfish flashing a ring (scare).

items.question: Draw a line graph of the made-up numbers from an Eyes in the Dark test: 1 minute, 3 sheets. 5 minutes, 5 sheets. 10 minutes, 7 sheets. 20 minutes, 9 sheets. Say what the line shows.
items.answer_should_show: A line that rises from 3 sheets at 1 minute to 9 sheets at 20 minutes, rising quickly at first and then more slowly. It shows that the longer the eyes are in the dark, the fainter a light they can see.

items.question: Draw a rod cell in the retina. Show a packet of light hitting a rhodopsin molecule and what happens next.
items.answer_should_show: A rod cell shaped like a tall rod, a small packet of light arriving at a rhodopsin molecule, the molecule changing from a bent shape to a straight one, and an arrow pointing to a nerve signal leaving the cell.

items.question: Draw a squid seen from below, with a light organ that has a lens and a shutter. Show moonlight coming down from above and show how the squid's shadow is cancelled.
items.answer_should_show: A squid with a glowing patch on the underside, a lens and shutter drawn on the patch, arrows of moonlight coming from above, and a note that the blue light from the patch makes the squid as bright as the water above, so the shadow vanishes.

items.question: Draw a torch, a flat mirror and an eye. Draw the path of the light from the torch to the mirror, then to the eye. Use a ruler.
items.answer_should_show: Two straight lines with arrows. One goes from the torch to the mirror. The other goes from the mirror to the eye, at the same angle on the other side.

items.question: You use a mirror to bounce sunlight onto a shady wall. Draw the Sun, the mirror and the bright spot on the wall, with arrows for the light. Then draw where the spot goes if you tilt the mirror a little.
items.answer_should_show: An arrow from the Sun to the mirror, and an arrow from the mirror to the spot on the wall. A second drawing shows the mirror tilted and the spot moved along the wall.

items.question: A mirror only half your height can show your whole body. Draw yourself standing in front of a mirror. Draw the light from the top of your head to the mirror and into your eyes, and the light from your feet to the mirror and into your eyes. Mark the part of the mirror you need.
items.answer_should_show: Two V-shaped light paths. Light from the head hits the mirror halfway between the head and the eyes, then goes to the eyes. Light from the feet hits the mirror halfway between the eyes and the feet. The part of the mirror between those two spots is half the body's height.

items.question: Design a sign for the back of a school bus that the driver behind can read normally. Then design a sign for the front of a van that the driver ahead can read in their rear-view mirror. Draw both signs as they must be painted.
items.answer_should_show: The back sign is painted the normal way, because the driver behind looks at it directly. The front sign is painted backwards, from right to left, with every letter turned round, like AMBULANCE.

items.question: Draw a side view of a periscope. Show the two mirrors, the two windows and the path of a ray of light from the top window to the eye.
items.answer_should_show: A tall tube with a window near the top on one face and a window near the bottom on the opposite face. A mirror sloping at 45 degrees behind each window, with shiny sides facing each other. A zigzag ray enters the top window, turns down, turns again and leaves the lower window.

items.question: Draw two mirrors at a right angle, a ray coming in and the ray going out. Show that the outgoing ray is parallel to the incoming ray.
items.answer_should_show: Two lines at a right angle, like the corner of a box, with the shiny sides facing in. A ray comes in, hits one mirror, then the other, and leaves going back parallel to the way it came in, with arrows drawn on each.

items.question: Draw a concave mirror and three parallel rays coming in. Show where the rays go after they bounce.
items.answer_should_show: A curved mirror with the hollow side facing the rays. Three parallel rays arrive. After bouncing, all three cross at one point in front of the mirror, called the focus.

items.question: Draw a kingfisher hovering straight above a fish in the water. Draw the light from the fish to the bird's eye. Is the light bent?
items.answer_should_show: The light goes straight up from the fish to the bird's eye, with no bend. So the fish is almost exactly below the spot the bird sees, only a little deeper.

items.question: Draw the March Like Light line walking from the mattress back onto the floor at a slant, seen from above. Add arrows for where they walk.
items.answer_should_show: The first person to step onto the floor speeds up, while the others are still slow. So the line swings round the other way, and walks on in a new direction, further from straight across the edge.

items.question: Draw a ray of light going at a slant into a thick block of clear glass and coming out of the other side. Show where it bends.
items.answer_should_show: The ray bends at the first edge, going in. It travels straight through the glass. It bends back at the second edge, coming out, and goes on in the same direction as before, only shifted sideways.

items.question: Draw a ray going at a slant into a glass block, through it, and out the other side. Draw the normal at both surfaces. Show how the ray bends.
items.answer_should_show: The ray bends toward the normal going in, goes straight in the glass, and bends away from the normal coming out. It leaves parallel to the way it came in, but shifted sideways.

items.question: Draw a curved optical fibre and show how a ray of light stays inside it. Mark one place where the ray bounces.
items.answer_should_show: A curved strip with a zigzag line inside it, touching the wall at shallow angles and bouncing off, with no light leaving the strip.

items.question: Draw a telescope from the side with its two lenses. Show light from the top of a faraway tree crossing through the tube and make the picture of the tree upside down.
items.answer_should_show: A tube with a big lens at the front and a small lens at the eye end. Rays from the top of the tree cross inside, so the top of the tree appears at the bottom of the picture.

items.question: Draw a torch, a ball and a wall. Then draw where the ball's shadow falls, and colour it dark.
items.answer_should_show: A torch on one side, the ball in the middle, and a round dark shadow on the wall behind the ball.

items.question: Draw a puppet with a hole for the eye. Next to it, draw its shadow on the wall. Show what the eye looks like in the shadow.
items.answer_should_show: A dark puppet shadow with a bright dot where the eye hole is.

items.question: Draw the shadow of a steel tumbler standing up, when a torch shines at it from the side. Then draw its shadow when the tumbler lies on its side with the open end facing the torch.
items.answer_should_show: Standing: a rectangle, a little wider at the top. Lying with the open end to the torch: a circle.

items.question: Draw a torch shining on one paper square, and on a pile of five squares. Draw arrows of light coming out of each.
items.answer_should_show: Many arrows come out of the one square. Only a few come out of the pile of five.

items.question: Draw the sea from the top to the bottom. Colour it bright at the top, dimmer in the middle and dark at the bottom. Draw one animal at the bottom, with the light she makes.
items.answer_should_show: Bright at the top, dim in the middle, black at the bottom, with a glowing animal deep down.

items.question: Draw light going down into the sea, with arrows. Draw many arrows at the top, fewer in the middle and none at the bottom.
items.answer_should_show: Many arrows at the surface, fewer lower down, and none at the bottom.

items.question: Draw a house with three windows. Make one window transparent, one translucent and one opaque. Draw what a person standing outside would see through each window.
items.answer_should_show: Through the transparent window, the person sees the room inside clearly. Through the translucent window, only a soft glow and blurry shapes. Through the opaque window, nothing at all.

items.question: Draw a window with a thin curtain twice: once in the day, and once at night with a lamp on inside. Show who can see whom.
items.answer_should_show: Day: the person inside can see the street, but the street sees only a bright curtain. Night: the street can see the person's shape, but the person sees only the curtain.

items.question: Draw a heap of clear sugar crystals and a ray of light zigzagging through it and coming out in many directions.
items.answer_should_show: A heap of many small shapes with a ray going in on one side, bouncing off several faces, and coming back out of the heap in different directions, some at the top and some at the sides.

items.question: Draw three windows in a row, each passing on nine tenths of the light. Write the share left after each one, starting from 100.
items.answer_should_show: Three panes in a row with arrows between them, labelled 100, 90, 81 and about 73.

items.question: Draw two polarising filters, one with upright bars and one with sideways bars, with a light wave arriving, wiggling up and down. Show where it goes through and where it stops.
items.answer_should_show: A wavy line passing through the filter with upright bars, and then stopped at the filter with sideways bars, with nothing coming out of the second filter.

items.question: Draw a torch, a piece of card with a small hole in the middle, and a wall behind it. Draw the path of the light from the torch, through the hole, to the wall.
items.answer_should_show: Straight lines go from the torch to the hole and carry on straight to the wall, making a small spot of light. Light that hits the card is blocked.

items.question: Draw the Late Moon act-out: the Sun in the middle, the Earth in two places on its path, and Jupiter with Io further out. Draw the path of light from Io to the Earth in each place, and mark which path is longer.
items.answer_should_show: Two straight lines from Io, one to the Earth on the near side of the Sun and one to the Earth on the far side. The far-side line is longer, so light takes longer and Io seems late.

items.question: Draw light as a wave and as photons in one picture. Label which part shows which idea.
items.answer_should_show: For example: a wavy line going across the page, with small dots placed along it, labelled 'travels like a wave' and 'arrives as packets (photons)'.

items.question: Draw a torch, a card with a small square hole in it, and a wall. Show the light spreading after the hole. Then show how the patch on a wall twice as far away would look.
items.answer_should_show: A torch on the left, the card in the middle, and two walls on the right, one near and one far. Straight lines spread out from the hole. The patch on the far wall is much bigger, about four times the area, and fainter.

items.question: Draw the light family as a long ribbon. Mark where radio waves, visible light and gamma rays go. Colour in the thin slice that your eyes can see.
items.answer_should_show: A long ribbon, with radio waves at the left end, then microwaves, infrared, a small rainbow slice for visible light, then ultraviolet, X-rays and gamma rays at the right end. The visible slice is very small.

items.question: Draw what happens to a beam of sunlight that lands on black paper, on white paper and on shiny foil. Use arrows to show the light that bounces and the light that is absorbed.
items.answer_should_show: Three beams arrive at three sheets. Black has an arrow in and almost nothing out, with wavy heat lines rising. White has an arrow in and a big arrow out, with a few heat lines. Foil has an arrow in and nearly the same arrow out, with almost no heat lines.

items.question: Draw a bar magnet that has been rolled in a heap of paper clips. Show where the clips cling. Label the north pole and the south pole.
items.answer_should_show: Bunches of clips at the two ends, labelled north and south, and few or none in the middle.

items.question: Draw two squares of iron as if you were looking from very, very close. In the first square, draw the tiny magnets as arrows for a plain nail. In the second, draw them for a magnet.
items.answer_should_show: Plain nail: patches of arrows, each patch pointing a different way. Magnet: nearly all the arrows pointing the same way.

items.question: Draw the Earth cut in half. Label the crust, the liquid outer core and the solid inner core. Draw curved magnetic field lines around the outside.
items.answer_should_show: A thin crust, a thick rocky middle, a liquid outer core and a solid inner core, with curved field lines looping from one pole round to the other.

items.question: Draw a magnet with a nail hanging from it and a paper clip hanging from the nail. Draw small arrows inside the nail and the clip to show which way their tiny magnets point.
items.answer_should_show: A magnet at the top, a nail below it and a clip below the nail. Inside the nail and the clip, small arrows all point the same way as the magnet's field.

items.question: Draw two nails hanging from one magnet in a V. Mark the pole at each head and at each tip, using N and S.
items.answer_should_show: A magnet at the top. Two nails hang below it in a V. If the magnet's pole at the heads is N, each head is S and each tip is N.

items.question: Draw two rafts, one with a magnet and one with a nail, at the start and after they have met. Show with arrows how far each raft moved when the nail raft is three times heavier.
items.answer_should_show: At the start, rafts 8 cm apart. After meeting, the magnet raft has moved about 6 cm and the heavy nail raft about 2 cm, with equal pull arrows between them at the start.

items.question: Draw two bar magnets that attract and two that repel. Label every pole N or S, and draw arrows to show which way each magnet is pushed or pulled.
items.answer_should_show: Attracting pair: N facing S, arrows pointing towards each other. Repelling pair: N facing N or S facing S, arrows pointing apart.

items.question: Draw three pictures of two floating magnet boats that start north facing north: at the start, halfway and at the end. Label the poles.
items.answer_should_show: Start: N facing N with a gap. Halfway: one boat turning. End: N of one touching S of the other, or side by side pointing opposite ways.

items.question: Draw the field lines around a bar magnet. Show where the lines are closest together.
items.answer_should_show: Curved lines leave the north pole, loop round the outside and enter the south pole. They are closest together near the poles.

items.question: Draw a bar magnet with its north pole facing the south pole of a second bar magnet. Draw the field lines in the gap between them.
items.answer_should_show: Lines leave the north pole and run straight across the gap into the south pole, bunched together.

items.question: Draw a bar magnet next to a thick iron tin. Show how the field lines bend into the wall of the tin.
items.answer_should_show: The lines from the magnet bend towards the tin and run along its walls. Few lines reach the inside.

items.question: Draw a burr's hook catching a loop of wool. Label the hook and the loop.
items.answer_should_show: A curved hook, like the letter J, caught through a round loop of wool, both labelled.
