items.question: Draw a water drop sitting on a lotus leaf, as if you could see it from the side, very close up. Show the bumps, the wax and the air.
items.answer_should_show: A round drop resting on the tips of bumps, a thin wax coat on each bump, and air in the gaps under the drop.

items.question: Invent something that copies a living thing you saw this week. Draw it, label the design you copied, and write how you would test it fairly.
items.answer_should_show: Any invention with a labelled design from a real living thing, and a fair test where only one thing changes.

items.question: Draw a foil boat that you think will carry many coins. Label the base and the walls, and write how tall the walls are.
items.answer_should_show: A wide, flat base with walls all the same height, about 2 to 4 centimetres tall, and tight corners.

items.question: Draw the design cycle as a loop with four arrows. Write one step on each arrow.
items.answer_should_show: A circle of four arrows: plan, build, test, improve, with improve leading back to plan or build.

items.question: Design a container to carry 2 idlis to school without squashing them, using only paper and string. Draw it and label how it protects the idlis.
items.answer_should_show: A strong design has stiff sides, for example folded or rolled paper, a lid, and a handle tied at strong points.

items.question: Draw a square frame. Then draw one strip that stops it leaning. Colour the two triangles it makes.
items.answer_should_show: A square with one diagonal from one corner to the opposite corner, with the two triangles coloured.

items.question: Draw a side view of a roof with four tiles overlapping the right way. Add arrows to show where rain runs.
items.answer_should_show: Four tiles in a slope, each higher tile lying over the top of the one below, with arrows running down over each tile and off the bottom edge.

items.question: Design a balcony shelter for a pigeon or a crow, using only sticks and string. Draw it and mark every triangle in red.
items.answer_should_show: Any shelter whose frame is split into triangles, with a roof sloping to shed rain, and an opening for the bird.

items.question: Draw a magnet held just above a paper clip, with a sheet of paper in between. Draw what the clip does.
items.answer_should_show: The clip has jumped up and is held against the underside of the paper, right below the magnet.

items.question: Draw two squares. In one, draw the tiny magnets inside wood as arrows. In the other, draw the tiny magnets inside a nail.
items.answer_should_show: In the wood square, the arrows are in pairs, and the two arrows in each pair point opposite ways. In the nail square, the arrows are in patches, and all the arrows in each patch point the same way.

items.question: Draw the Earth cut in half. Label the solid inner core, the liquid outer core, the mantle and the crust.
items.answer_should_show: A circle with four layers. In the middle, a small circle labelled solid inner core. Around it, a thick ring labelled liquid outer core. Then a thick ring of mantle, and a thin outer ring of crust.

items.question: Draw a flat aluminium plate with a magnet moving above it. Draw curved arrows in the plate to show the swirls of current, and an arrow to show which way the magnet moves.
items.answer_should_show: A flat plate with a magnet above it and an arrow for its motion. Inside the plate, curved loops of arrows swirl under the magnet.

items.question: Draw a conveyor belt with four stations in a good order: a magnet, a spinning magnet drum, an air blower and hands. Label what each station takes out.
items.answer_should_show: A belt starting with a heap. The magnet comes first and takes out steel. Then the drum throws off aluminium and other non-ferrous metals. The blower lifts light paper. Hands pick the rest.

items.question: Draw your kitchen map in three zones: sticks firmly, sticks weakly, does not stick. Put at least two things in each zone, and write the name of one thing that surprised you.
items.answer_should_show: Three labelled zones. Typical: sticks firmly, a steel pan base and a tawa. Sticks weakly, a tumbler rim. Does not stick, an aluminium kadai, a brass lamp and a glass jar.

items.question: Draw the heap of sugar and the cooled sugar sheet, each on top of a word in the newspaper.
items.answer_should_show: The heap hides the word. The word can be read through the sheet.

items.question: Draw the journey of a glass bangle, from the beach to a wrist. Draw at least three steps.
items.answer_should_show: Sand, then a furnace melting it, then a worker pulling or shaping hot glass, then a bangle on a wrist.

items.question: Draw the Torch Spot Test: the torch, the steel plate and the bright spot on the wall.
items.answer_should_show: A torch shining at a slant onto a plate, and a bright spot on the wall.

items.question: Draw one rough thing and one smooth thing from your home. Draw bumps on the rough one.
items.answer_should_show: Two drawings, such as a doormat with bumps and a steel plate with none.

items.question: A girl sees the sky in a river. Draw the river when it is still. Then draw it just after a boat goes past.
items.answer_should_show: A still river with the sky in it, and a rippled river with the sky broken into pieces.

items.question: Draw the tumbler with polythene on top, and the tumbler with the tea strainer on top, after you poured the water. Show where the water ended up.
items.answer_should_show: Water sitting in a little pool on the polythene with a dry tumbler below. Water at the bottom of the tumbler under the strainer.

items.question: Design a monsoon suit for a superhero. Label one part that is waterproof, one that is stretchy, one that is strong and one that is see-through.
items.answer_should_show: For example, a waterproof polythene cape, stretchy rubber cuffs, a strong cotton belt and a see-through plastic face shield.

items.question: Draw one object from your kitchen. Write its material next to it. Then label three properties of that material, and how you found each one out.
items.answer_should_show: Any kitchen object with its correct material and three true properties. For example, a steel tumbler: shiny (I see my face in it), hard (my fingernail cannot scratch it), waterproof (water stays inside).

items.question: Draw a torch beam meeting three materials: clear glass, butter paper and a steel plate. Show what the light does in each.
items.answer_should_show: Clear glass: the beam goes straight through. Butter paper: the beam goes in but spreads out in all directions. Steel plate: the beam stops or bounces back.

items.question: Draw a zoom-in: a cotton thread, then one fibre, then a pattern of atoms joined together. Label the three pictures.
items.answer_should_show: A thread made of many fibres twisted together. One fibre as a long thin strand. At the smallest scale, tiny balls joined in chains.

items.question: Draw a sheet of newspaper with a straight tear and a crooked tear. Draw an arrow for the grain direction, and write how you could tell which way it runs.
items.answer_should_show: A sheet with a straight tear running one way and a ragged tear running the other way. A grain arrow along the straight tear, and a note such as: I tear the paper both ways and see which tear runs straight.

items.question: Draw the inside of a plywood sheet with three layers, seen from the side. Draw a small arrow or a dotted line on each layer to show which way its grain runs.
items.answer_should_show: Three thin layers, drawn as three bands. The top and bottom layers have the grain drawn as lines along the board, and the middle layer has dots or circles, to show grain coming towards the viewer, or a different pattern to show it is turned across.

items.question: Draw an I-shaped steel beam from the end. Mark where the thick parts are, and write one sentence on why this shape is stiff.
items.answer_should_show: An I shape with a thick bar at the top, a thick bar at the bottom and a thin web joining them. A sentence such as: Most of the steel is far from the middle, where it does the most work against a bend.

items.question: Draw a bucket of water. Draw the steel spoon where it ended up, and the steel katori where it ended up.
items.answer_should_show: The spoon at the bottom of the bucket, and the katori floating on top.

items.question: Draw something at home that is made of two materials. Colour each material a different colour.
items.answer_should_show: For example, a pressure cooker with a metal pot and a black plastic handle, in two colours.

items.question: Draw a new thing made of steel that you think would float. Show the air inside it.
items.answer_should_show: For example, a steel tiffin box with its lid shut, a steel plate, or a steel boat, with the air coloured in.

items.question: Draw a Venn diagram with two circles, 'Round' and 'Red'. Put four things in it.
items.answer_should_show: Two overlapping circles. A tomato or a red ball in the overlap. A red book in Red only. A coin in Round only. A pencil outside.

items.question: Draw a Carroll table with the rules 'Is it made of metal?' and 'Does it float in water?'. Put one thing from home in each of the four boxes.
items.answer_should_show: For example: metal and floats, an empty steel bowl or a foil boat. Metal and sinks, a steel spoon or a nail. Not metal and floats, a wooden spoon or a plastic bottle cap. Not metal and sinks, a stone or a glass marble.

items.question: Draw a branching key for four fruits: mango, banana, guava, apple. Use yes or no questions.
items.answer_should_show: For example, 'Do you peel it before eating?' Yes gives mango or banana, split by 'Is it long and curved?'. No gives guava or apple, split by 'Is it red outside?'.

items.question: Draw a ladder of five things you know, in order by a number. Draw two different cut-offs on it, and show how each one makes different groups.
items.answer_should_show: A ladder of five things in order, such as five children by height, or five foods by mass. Two lines drawn across it at different places, with the groups named on each side. At least one thing changes group between the two lines.

items.question: Invent five foods and two numbers for each. Draw a map of the five dots, label the axes, and ring any clump you find.
items.answer_should_show: A map with two labelled axes, five dots each with a food name, and a ring round any dots that sit close together. The numbers must be plausible for the foods.

items.question: Draw a seesaw. Label one end wrongly kept back and the other wrongly let through. Show a hand moving a cut-off marker underneath, and what happens to the seesaw.
items.answer_should_show: A seesaw with the two kinds of mistake on the two ends, a cut-off marker under it, and the seesaw tipped one way. Moving the marker tips the seesaw the other way. One kind goes down and the other goes up.

items.question: Draw the rubber band before the bottle, with the bottle, and after the bottle came off.
items.answer_should_show: Three pictures: a short band, a long band with a bottle, and a short band again.

items.question: Draw something in your home that must be waterproof. Write what it is made of.
items.answer_should_show: For example, an umbrella made of umbrella cloth, a bucket made of plastic, or a steel tumbler.

items.question: Draw what you think rubber looks like inside, when it is loose and when it is stretched.
items.answer_should_show: Loose: curly, tangled lines. Stretched: the same lines pulled straighter.

items.question: Draw an empty results table for the width test. It tests three strips 2 cm wide and three strips 4 cm wide. Give each column a heading with a unit.
items.answer_should_show: Columns: Strip, Try 1 (coins), Try 2 (coins), Try 3 (coins), Middle value (coins), Where it tore. Two rows: 2 cm wide and 4 cm wide.

items.question: Draw what you think the edge of a torn kitchen towel looks like under a magnifying glass. Then draw the edge of torn printer paper.
items.answer_should_show: The kitchen towel edge is fluffy, with loose fibres and big gaps. The printer paper edge is neater, with fibres pressed tightly together and few gaps.

items.question: Draw a dot plot for these five bounce heights, in centimetres: 30, 32, 32, 33, 35.
items.answer_should_show: A number line from 30 to 35. One dot above 30, two dots stacked above 32, one dot above 33 and one dot above 35. The range is 5 centimetres.

items.question: Draw two targets. On the first, show arrows that are precise but not accurate. On the second, show arrows that are accurate on average but not precise. Label each one.
items.answer_should_show: First target: all arrows in a tight group off to one side. Second target: arrows spread widely, but scattered evenly around the middle.

items.question: Draw a plan for a blind test of two kinds of tissue paper. Show who does what, and how the order is chosen.
items.answer_should_show: A helper tags 10 pieces of each kind with secret letters and keeps the list. The tester draws chits to set the order, tests each piece the same way, and writes the number against its letter. At the end the helper opens the list and the numbers are sorted into two dot plots.

items.question: Draw a child going out in the rain. Give the child a coat that keeps them dry. Colour the coat.
items.answer_should_show: A drawing of a child in a raincoat, with rain falling.

items.question: Draw a boat that would not go soft in a puddle. Tell a grown-up what it is made of.
items.answer_should_show: A drawing of a boat made of plastic, foil or another material that keeps water out.

items.question: Draw something at home that is made of glass. Tell a grown-up its job.
items.answer_should_show: A drawing of a glass thing, such as a window, a jar or a tumbler, with its job said aloud.

items.question: Draw the tilted board with the katori sitting on the rubber bands. Draw an arrow to show which way the katori would slide.
items.answer_should_show: A board with one end lifted, the katori on it, and an arrow pointing down the slope.

items.question: Draw a silly tray mat made of a very slippery material. Show what happens to the tumblers.
items.answer_should_show: A tray with a shiny plastic mat and tumblers sliding off.

items.question: Design a tray for a tea seller who carries tumblers of tea through a moving train. Label the material on top and say why you chose it.
items.answer_should_show: A tray with a rubber mat, or holes for each tumbler, labelled with the material and the reason.

items.question: Draw your school bag. Label three materials it is made of. Next to each label, write the job that material does.
items.answer_should_show: For example: cloth or nylon for the body, because it is strong and light. A plastic or metal zip, because it is stiff and slides. Foam in the straps, because it is soft on the shoulders.

items.question: A fruit seller in a hot market wants to keep her grapes cool all day, with no electricity. Design a cooler for her. Draw it, and label each material and its job.
items.answer_should_show: For example: a big clay pot with a smaller clay pot inside it. Wet sand fills the gap. A wet cloth covers the top. Labels say the clay is porous, the water in the sand evaporates and takes heat away, and the cooler stands in the shade where air can move.

items.question: Draw two zoom-ins side by side, as if you had a super microscope. One shows the atoms in a steel spoon. The other shows the atoms in a wooden spoon. Show why heat moves faster through steel.
items.answer_should_show: The steel side shows neat rows of atoms, with tiny dots, the free electrons, moving between them, and long arrows for heat. The wooden side shows atoms with no free dots, and short arrows for heat creeping slowly.

items.question: Draw the life of a cotton shirt in four boxes in a circle, from source to after. Write one thing in each box.
items.answer_should_show: Source: a cotton field. Making: a mill and a tailor. Use: worn and washed many times. After: mended, passed on, or rotting in soil. Arrows go round the circle.

items.question: Draw a mud brick with straw in it, and show a crack starting from one side. Show where the crack stops, and say why.
items.answer_should_show: A rectangle with straw lines through it. A crack starts at an edge and stops when it meets a straw fibre. The fibre carries the pull and stops the crack from running through.

items.question: Draw the life of a plastic bottle in four boxes in a circle. Add a second arrow to show it being remade, and a third to show it staying in the ground.
items.answer_should_show: Source: oil or gas from the ground. Making: a factory. Use: a drink, a few days. After: three arrows, one to a recycling plant back to a new bottle, one to a landfill, and one to a river.

items.question: Draw something in your home that is made of glass. Draw a ring around the glass part.
items.answer_should_show: A drawing of a window, a mirror, a jar or a bottle, with a ring around the glass.

items.question: Draw one thing at home that is made of two materials. Colour each material in a different colour.
items.answer_should_show: For example, a knife with a steel blade and a plastic handle, coloured in two colours.

items.question: Draw the newspaper cone from the Paper Cup Puzzle, one minute after the water went in.
items.answer_should_show: A dark, soft-looking cone with drops of water falling onto a plate.

items.question: Draw a cotton shirt in the middle of a page. Around it, draw where its material came from, and two people who helped to make it.
items.answer_should_show: For example: a cotton plant in a field, a farmer picking the fluff, a spinner at a spinning wheel and a weaver at a loom, with arrows to the shirt.

items.question: In the project, you shook soil and water in a bottle and let it settle. Draw the layers you saw, and label them.
items.answer_should_show: Pebbles and sand at the bottom, then silt, then smooth clay, then cloudy or clear water at the top.

items.question: Draw the journey of one iron atom in four pictures: made inside a star, thrown into space, part of the young Earth, and now in your steel kadai.
items.answer_should_show: Four boxes with arrows: a bright star, an explosion scattering dust, a rocky young Earth, and a kadai on a stove, with a dot for the same atom in each.

items.question: Draw yourself and one person from your home, side by side. Circle one thing that is the same about you.
items.answer_should_show: Two people, with a circle round something they share, such as two eyes or ten fingers.

items.question: Draw one kind thing you can do for someone at home today.
items.answer_should_show: Any kind act, such as carrying a bag, sharing a snack or giving a hug.

items.question: Draw a snack plate with something on it for every person at home. Write or say who each snack is for.
items.answer_should_show: A plate with several different snacks and a name next to each.

items.question: Draw a tumbler and a banana on a table as you see them. Then draw them as someone on the other side of the table would see them.
items.answer_should_show: Two drawings. In the second, the banana is on the other side of the tumbler, and anything hidden in the first may now be in view.

items.question: Draw your room the way an ant on the floor would see the room. Then write one thing the ant can see that you never notice.
items.answer_should_show: A drawing from very low down: huge table legs, chappals, the underside of the bed. One noticed thing, such as dust or a crumb under the cupboard.

items.question: Draw a picture plan of a shared space in a block of flats, such as the play area, that works for a child in a wheelchair, a grandmother and a toddler.
items.answer_should_show: A plan with a ramp, benches in the shade, a low fence round a toddler area and wide paths.

items.question: Draw a germ chain in your home with four links. Then draw a pair of scissors cutting one link.
items.answer_should_show: Any chain with an ill person, a way out, a ride and a next person, with one link cut.

items.question: Draw a germ chain for an illness that travels in water: from a sick person, to dirty waste, to a well, to the people who drink from it. Then draw where you could break the chain.
items.answer_should_show: A chain of pictures joined by arrows, with a break marked, for example at the well or the pump.

items.question: Draw nine houses in a square, three rows of three. Colour one house red for an ill house. Then colour the neighbours of that house to show vaccinated houses, and show where the illness is stopped.
items.answer_should_show: A drawing in which the vaccinated houses surround the ill house, and arrows from the ill house are stopped at them.

items.question: Draw how a velvet stamp copies a pattern of dots from one dish of bacteria to two new dishes. Show which dish has the medicine in it.
items.answer_should_show: A drawing of a dish with dots, a round velvet pad pressed on it, then pressed on two new dishes where the same pattern of dots appears, one with a label for the medicine.

items.question: Draw a germ chain for a bacterial illness that spreads through water. Mark three places where clean water, a toilet or a vaccine could break the chain.
items.answer_should_show: A chain of pictures from an ill person to dirty water to a drinker, with three marked breaks such as a toilet that keeps waste away from the water, boiling or filtering the water, and a vaccine for the next person.

items.question: Draw a yeast cell with a small bud. Then draw a piece of dough with bubbles of carbon dioxide inside.
items.answer_should_show: A round cell with a smaller round bump growing from it, and a piece of dough with several round bubbles inside.

items.question: Draw a bowl of curd with a spoon. Then draw a circle zoomed in on one drop, showing bacteria turning milk sugar into lactic acid.
items.answer_should_show: A bowl of curd with a spoon, and a zoomed circle with small rod-shaped bacteria and arrows from a sugar to an acid.

items.question: Draw how one spoon of starter curd passes from an old pot of curd into a new pot of milk, and show what happens to the bacteria over the night.
items.answer_should_show: An old pot with a spoon, an arrow to a new pot of milk, and bacteria drawn few at the start and many at the end.

items.question: Draw the three potato slices from your test on the last day. Draw every spot you saw.
items.answer_should_show: Three slices. The soil slice has the most spots, the finger slice has some spots near the fingerprints, and the Nobody slice has the fewest.

items.question: Draw what you think one spot on the potato looks like through a very strong microscope.
items.answer_should_show: Many tiny cells packed together, round or rod-shaped, or long thin threads for mould.

items.question: Draw a map of your body. Put dots where microbes live: skin, mouth, tummy and anywhere else you think.
items.answer_should_show: A body outline with dots on the skin, in the mouth, in the tummy and on the hands.

items.question: Draw a head louse holding a hair, with an egg glued near the scalp.
items.answer_should_show: A small insect with six legs, each ending in a claw round the hair, and a small oval egg on the hair close to the scalp.

items.question: Draw the malaria journey as a circle with four arrows: person, mosquito stomach, mosquito saliva, new person.
items.answer_should_show: A circle of four labelled stages joined by arrows, in that order.

items.question: Design a sign for your building's notice board that tells neighbours how to stop mosquitoes breeding. Use pictures and at most 10 words.
items.answer_should_show: For example: a bucket with a lid, an empty flowerpot saucer and the words 'Empty and cover water every Sunday'.

items.question: Draw a circle of arrows that shows a parasite going from one host to a second host and back to the first. Mark one place where you would cut the circle.
items.answer_should_show: A circle with two hosts, for example a person and a copepod or a mosquito, joined by arrows, with a scissors mark on one arrow.

items.question: Draw a circle of arrows showing how a person with a Guinea worm blister can infect other people through a village well. Then mark two places where you would cut it.
items.answer_should_show: A circle of arrows: foot, water, copepod, mouth, person, with two marks, such as a cloth on the pot and a sore foot kept out of the well.

items.question: Draw a funnel that starts with 1,000 eggs. At each of four gates, half of the eggs are lost. Write the number of eggs left after every gate.
items.answer_should_show: 1,000 at the top, then 500, 250, 125, and about 62 at the bottom.

items.question: Draw the four tickle faces you used, from 0 to 3.
items.answer_should_show: A straight face for 0, a small smile for 1, a big smile for 2 and a laughing face for 3.

items.question: Draw yourself looking in a mirror with a sticker on your right cheek. Draw where the sticker is on the mirror you.
items.answer_should_show: In the mirror, the sticker is on the side of the mirror girl's face that is nearest your own right hand. In a photo it is on the other side.

items.question: Draw a machine that could let you tickle yourself. Label the part you move and the part that touches your foot.
items.answer_should_show: A drawing with labels, for example a string over a chair with a feather on one end.

items.question: Draw two neurons with a gap between them. Draw an arrow to show which way the message goes.
items.answer_should_show: Two neurons, each with a round middle, branches and a tail. The tail of the first is close to a branch of the second, with a small gap. The arrow goes along the first neuron's tail, across the gap, into the second.

items.question: Draw the shape of the line graph you would expect for ten tries of writing with your other hand. Label the bottom 'try' and the side 'seconds'. Write one sentence about the shape.
items.answer_should_show: A line that starts high, falls quickly over the first few tries, then falls more slowly. 'I got faster quickly at first, then more slowly.'

items.question: Draw the Roll or Slide Test: the dabba on its side and the dabba standing flat. Draw a long line for the one that went further.
items.answer_should_show: The dabba on its side with a long line, and the dabba standing flat with a short line.

items.question: Draw one thing in your kitchen that rolls, and one that swings.
items.answer_should_show: For example, a lemon or rolling pin that rolls, and a ladle on a hook that swings.

items.question: Draw the bag swinging on the door handle. Put a dot on the part that stays still.
items.answer_should_show: A bag hanging below a handle, with a dot on the handle and a curved arrow under it.

items.question: Draw a new toy that can roll, spin and bounce. Show with arrows how it does each one.
items.answer_should_show: Any toy, such as a ball, with an arrow for rolling, a curved arrow for spinning, and an up arrow for bouncing.

items.question: Draw the keys on a string as you saw them from above. Then draw them as you saw them from the side. Draw the path each time.
items.answer_should_show: From above: keys with a circle round them. From the side: keys with a straight line and arrows at both ends.

items.question: Draw the path of the tip of a fan blade, as you see it lying under the fan. Then draw what a gecko on the wall, level with the fan, would see.
items.answer_should_show: From below: a circle. From the wall: a straight line with arrows at both ends.

items.question: Nisha, a girl in Class 2, says a ball lying still will start rolling by itself if you wait long enough. Draw how you would test this. What do you expect to see?
items.answer_should_show: A ball on a flat floor and a clock. The ball stays still until something pushes it or the floor slopes.

items.question: Your helper watched the walking drop from the side. Draw the path of the rolled socks through the air, from your hand to the floor. Draw the plate too.
items.answer_should_show: A curve that starts at the hand, goes forward and down, and lands past the plate.

items.question: Draw a view from above of a bus turning left. Show with an arrow which way a standing passenger leans.
items.answer_should_show: A bus curving to the left, with an arrow on the passenger pointing to the right, towards the outside of the turn.

items.question: Design a safety feature for a school bus that would protect children if it braked suddenly. Draw it and label how it works.
items.answer_should_show: Any sensible design, such as seatbelts, high padded seat backs, or soft bars in front of each seat, with labels saying how it stops children safely.

items.question: Draw two carts pulled by the same bag of water, one empty and one loaded with a bottle. Draw a longer arrow beside the cart that speeds up more every second.
items.answer_should_show: Two carts side by side, each with a thread to a bag. The empty cart has the longer arrow.

items.question: Draw a cyclist riding at a steady speed along a flat road. Draw the forces along the road as arrows. Make the arrows the right lengths.
items.answer_should_show: A cyclist with an arrow pointing forward and an arrow of the same length pointing back.

items.question: A fielder catches a fast ball. Draw two catches side by side, one with hands that do not move back and one with hands that move back. Mark which catch has the longer stop.
items.answer_should_show: Two pictures of a fielder. In the second, the hands are drawn moving back with an arrow, and the second catch is marked as the longer stop.

items.question: Draw the path of a ball thrown gently from your hand to a friend's hands across the room.
items.answer_should_show: A smooth curve that rises from the thrower's hand, bends over and comes down to the catcher's hands.

items.question: Draw a table from the side. Draw the paths of two marbles rolling off it: one slow and one fast. Show where each lands.
items.answer_should_show: Two curves starting at the table edge. The slow one curves down steeply and lands close to the table. The fast one goes further out before curving down and lands further away.

items.question: Draw three throws from the same hand at the same speed: nearly flat, halfway up, and nearly straight up. Show where each lands.
items.answer_should_show: The nearly flat throw lands close. The nearly straight up throw goes high and lands close. The halfway throw lands furthest away.

items.question: Design a shoe for running on a beach. Draw it and label two features that help on soft sand.
items.answer_should_show: A drawing with features such as a wide sole so the foot sinks less, or a grippy bottom so the sand doesn't slide away. Each feature is labelled with what it does.

items.question: Draw two footprint trails across the same room: one with tiny steps and one with your ordinary steps.
items.answer_should_show: Two trails of the same length. The tiny-step trail has many footprints close together. The ordinary trail has fewer footprints, further apart.

items.question: Draw the Head-Start Race path. Show both start lines, the near finish, the far finish and the place where you caught up.
items.answer_should_show: A line with the child's start at the back, the grown-up's start ahead, the near finish just past the grown-up's start, the catch-up mark a little further, and the far finish beyond it.

items.question: Draw a race that is NOT fair. Then draw a cross on what makes it unfair, and write how to fix it.
items.answer_should_show: For example, one runner starting halfway, crossed out, with the words 'start at the same line'.

items.question: Draw a spinning top from the side. Draw a dotted line for its axis, and a dotted circle to show the path of its head when it leans.
items.answer_should_show: A top with a straight dotted line from tip to handle, slightly leaning, and a circle above the handle.

items.question: Draw a merry-go-round from above. Show the path of a rider near the pole and the path of a rider on the outside. Which path is longer?
items.answer_should_show: Two circles round a middle dot: a small one near the pole and a big one at the edge. The big circle is longer.

items.question: Draw a ring and a solid disc of the same size. Shade where most of the weight is in each. Then draw an arrow to show which would win a race down a slope.
items.answer_should_show: The ring shaded only round the edge; the disc shaded all over. The arrow points to the disc as the winner.

items.question: Draw a stone going round on a string. Mark the point where the string snaps, and draw the straight path the stone takes afterwards.
items.answer_should_show: A circle with a stone on it, and a straight line leaving the circle at the point where the string snaps, touching the circle.

items.question: Draw a cyclist taking a bend to the left. Show which way the cyclist leans, and draw an arrow for the push of the ground on the cycle.
items.answer_should_show: A cyclist leaning to the left, towards the inside of the bend, with an arrow from the ground pointing inward and up through the cycle.

items.question: A wet umbrella is spinning, with its rim going round anticlockwise. Draw the umbrella from above, and show the path of a drop of water as it leaves the rim.
items.answer_should_show: A circle for the umbrella, and a drop leaving the rim along a straight line that touches the circle, in the direction the rim was moving.

items.question: Draw a pendulum at the start, the middle and the far end of one swing. Draw a long arrow where it moves fastest and no arrow where it stops.
items.answer_should_show: A long arrow at the bottom and no arrows at the two ends.

items.question: Draw a parent pushing a child on a swing at the best moment. Draw an arrow for the push and an arrow for the way the swing is moving.
items.answer_should_show: The parent pushes at the back of the swing, as it starts to move away. Both arrows point the same way.

items.question: Draw a graph with length on the bottom and the time for 10 swings up the side. Plot 12 and a half cm at 7 seconds, 25 cm at 10 seconds and 50 cm at 14 seconds. Join the points. Is it a straight line?
items.answer_should_show: The points rise, but the line bends and gets flatter. It is not a straight line.

items.question: Draw a bob swinging past a peg. Draw a dotted line to show how high it starts and how high it reaches on the other side.
items.answer_should_show: The dotted line is at the same height on both sides, even though the path on one side is tighter.

items.question: Draw a graph of the height energy and the movement energy of a bob during one swing from the left end to the right end. Use two lines.
items.answer_should_show: The height energy line is high at the ends and low in the middle. The movement energy line is low at the ends and high in the middle. They mirror each other.

items.question: Draw a pendulum, a peg and the two paths of the bob on either side of the peg. Label the long side and the short side, and write how their times compare.
items.answer_should_show: The long side is drawn as a wide arc, the short side as a tighter arc. The short side is labelled as a quicker half-swing.

items.question: Draw a number line from 0 to 10. Show, with one mark, that the numbers go on after 10.
items.answer_should_show: A straight line with 0 to 10 evenly spaced, and an arrow at the end after 10.

items.question: Draw a picture that shows the difference between 'very many' and 'infinite'.
items.answer_should_show: For example: a heap of rice labelled 'very many', and a number line with an arrow labelled 'infinite'.

items.question: Draw a cartoon in three boxes: someone tries to count to infinity, and what happens.
items.answer_should_show: For example: box 1, a girl starts '1, 2, 3'. Box 2, she is tired at '1,23,451'. Box 3, she sees the numbers still going on past the edge of the picture.

items.question: Draw three katoris that show 407. Label each katori and draw the beans.
items.answer_should_show: Three katoris labelled Hundreds, Tens and Ones, with 4 beans, no beans and 7 beans.

items.question: Draw a number line from -4 to 4. Mark where you would be if you start at 1 and go down 3.
items.answer_should_show: A line with -4 to 4 evenly spaced, and a mark on -2.

items.question: Draw a number line from -5 to 5. A night in Leh starts at 3 °C, drops 4 degrees, then rises 2 degrees. Mark where it ends.
items.answer_should_show: A line with -5 to 5 evenly spaced, and a mark on 1.

items.question: Draw your domino line with the widest gap, after you pushed the first one. Show which dominoes fell and which stayed standing.
items.answer_should_show: One domino lying flat, its top just reaching the bottom of the next one, and nine dominoes still standing.

items.question: Draw the coin line before and after you slid two coins in together. Put an arrow on each coin that moved away.
items.answer_should_show: A line of five coins with two coins coming in at one end, and then two coins sliding away from the far end.

items.question: Draw a plan for a machine where one push starts four causes in a row, and the last one rings a steel bowl. Put an arrow from each cause to its effect.
items.answer_should_show: A drawing with at least four parts, such as dominoes, a ruler see-saw, a rolling marble and a steel bowl, each joined by an arrow.

items.question: Draw your tally from the coin test. Show the heads row and the tails row.
items.answer_should_show: Two rows of tally lines, in bundles of five, of nearly the same length.

items.question: Draw two tumblers of slips: one where a star is likely, and one where a star and a blank are just as likely.
items.answer_should_show: One tumbler with many star slips and few blank ones. One tumbler with the same number of each.

items.question: Draw the newspaper from your paper leaf test. Put a red cross where the ball landed and a blue cross where the leaf landed.
items.answer_should_show: Red crosses bunched in or near the circle, and blue crosses spread out all over the paper.

items.question: Draw a splash from 30 centimetres and a splash from one metre. Show how they were different.
items.answer_should_show: A small splash with a few little dots, and a bigger splash with more spikes and many more dots.

items.question: Draw a tree where every branch splits into two shorter branches. Go at least four levels.
items.answer_should_show: A trunk splitting into 2, then 4, then 8, then 16 branch tips.

items.question: Draw the pattern left by paint pulled apart between two sheets. Then draw an arrow to show where the air pushed in.
items.answer_should_show: A branching, tree-like pattern, with arrows pointing in from the edge along the fingers.

items.question: Draw a Koch curve starting from a line 9 centimetres long. Draw the line, then round 1, and write the length after each.
items.answer_should_show: A 9 centimetre line, then the same line with a tent of two 3 centimetre sides in the middle third. The lengths are 9 and 12 centimetres.

items.question: Draw a tree where every branch splits into two shorter branches, with three levels of splitting. Count the tips.
items.answer_should_show: A trunk that splits into 2, then 4, then 8 branches, so there are 8 tips.

items.question: Draw a spiral that grows by adding the same amount each turn, and a spiral that grows by multiplying by the same fraction. Label which is which.
items.answer_should_show: A rope-like coil with equal gaps labelled adding, and a shell-like spiral with gaps growing wider labelled multiplying.

items.question: Here is half a butterfly, next to a dotted line. Draw the other half, so the two sides match. Then colour both sides the same.
items.answer_should_show: A whole butterfly, with the same wing shapes and spots on both sides of the dotted line.

items.question: Draw your own face, looking in a mirror. Draw a line down the middle. Then draw one thing that is a little different on your two sides.
items.answer_should_show: A face with a line down the nose, and one small difference marked, such as one eyebrow higher or a mole on one cheek.

items.question: Draw a kolam or a rangoli that is the same on both sides of a line. Check it with a mirror.
items.answer_should_show: A pattern with a line down the middle, where each loop or dot on one side has a matching one on the other side.

items.question: Draw a shape that has exactly one line of symmetry and no rotational symmetry. Then draw a shape that has rotational symmetry but no line of symmetry.
items.answer_should_show: For example, a butterfly or a heart for the first, and the letter S, the letter Z or a pinwheel for the second.

items.question: Draw a fish from the side and from above. On the view from above, draw her line of symmetry.
items.answer_should_show: A fish from above with a line running from her mouth to her tail.

items.question: Design a tile that can cover a floor with no gaps, and draw how 6 of them fit together.
items.answer_should_show: Any shape that fits without gaps: a square, an equal triangle, a hexagon, or a cleverer shape.

items.question: Draw a badge that has exactly 2 symmetries and no mirror line. Say what it is.
items.answer_should_show: For example the letter S or a yin-yang symbol, which fit back after the do-nothing move and a half turn only.

items.question: Draw a border made of three copies of the letter F using a glide. Mark the line each F is flipped across.
items.answer_should_show: An upright F, then an upside-down mirror F slid along, then an upright F slid further along, with a dotted line running along the middle of the border.

items.question: Draw one pattern with a half turn symmetry and no mirror line. Draw another pattern with a mirror line and no half turn.
items.answer_should_show: For example the letter S for the first, and an isosceles triangle or a leaf shape for the second.

items.question: Draw a steel plate, a pencil and a cup on a table, as a bird would see them from straight above.
items.answer_should_show: A circle for the plate, a long thin rectangle for the pencil, and a smaller circle for the cup.

items.question: Draw a map of your bedroom from above. Include a key with at least four symbols and a north arrow.
items.answer_should_show: A box for the room with gaps for the door and window, symbols for the bed, cupboard and other things, a key that explains every symbol, and an N arrow.

items.question: Draw a map of a room where 'forward 2 tiles, then right 3 tiles' and '2 tiles north, then 3 tiles east' lead to the same tile. Mark which way the walker must face at the start.
items.answer_should_show: A grid with the start, the coin 2 tiles north and 3 east, and an arrow showing the walker faces north at the start.

items.question: Design a map symbol for each of these: a school, a hospital, a temple and a bus stop. Then draw a key for them.
items.answer_should_show: Four simple symbols, each easy to draw small and different from the others, and a key naming each one.

items.question: Draw the Hidden Hills box from above with 6 holes marked and a narrow ridge hiding between them. Show which holes would miss it.
items.answer_should_show: A rectangle with six dots in a pattern and a thin ridge drawn in the gap between the dots, not under any of them.

items.question: Draw three towers, three circles and the one place where they all meet. Mark where the coin is.
items.answer_should_show: Three dots for towers, three circles around them, all three circles meeting at a single point where a coin is drawn.

items.question: A sea survey must find any hill that is 2 squares wide and 2 squares long on a map of 8 by 8 squares. Mark the squares you would sound to be sure of finding one.
items.answer_should_show: Sound every second square in every second row, for example B2, B4, B6, B8, D2, D4, D6, D8, F2, F4, F6, F8, H2, H4, H6, H8, so that every 2 by 2 block of squares has a sounding in it.

items.question: A piece of chalk is shaken many times in a closed tiffin with stone chips. Draw it before shaking and after shaking. Show the corners clearly.
items.answer_should_show: A sharp-cornered piece, then a rounded piece with no sharp corners.

items.question: Draw a small patch of granite as it looks close up. Colour each kind of grain.
items.answer_should_show: A square full of grains in three or four colours, such as black, white, pink and grey.

items.question: Design a test to find out whether salt crystals or chalk pieces get round faster. Draw your test and label what you keep the same.
items.answer_should_show: A drawing of two tiffins, the same number of pieces, the same number of shakes, with labels.

items.question: Draw your soil jar the day after you shook it. Label the sand, the silt, the clay, the water and the floating bits.
items.answer_should_show: Sand at the bottom, then a finer silt layer, then a thin clay layer, then water that is clearer, with dark bits floating at the top.

items.question: Draw a cut-away of soil under a tree. Show fallen leaves on top, humus below them, an earthworm tunnel and a root.
items.answer_should_show: Leaves on the surface, a dark humus layer below, a worm in a tunnel, and a root growing down.

items.question: Draw two hill slopes after heavy rain: one bare and one with plants. Show what the rain does to each.
items.answer_should_show: On the bare slope, brown water and soil run down. On the planted slope, the water is clearer and soaks in around the roots.

items.question: Design a balcony box that turns your family's fallen leaves and peels into humus. Draw it and label how air, water and worms or other decomposers get in.
items.answer_should_show: A box or bucket with holes for air, a lid against rain, layers of peels and dry leaves, and a tray underneath for drips.

items.question: Draw your Salty Seeds test on day 3. Show the four saucers and how many seeds sprouted in each.
items.answer_should_show: Four saucers in a row. The plain saucer has the most sprouted seeds, the pinch of salt saucer has a few less, the half spoon saucer has very few and the one spoon saucer has none.

items.question: Draw a field with a white salt crust on top. Show where the water came from, where it went and where the salt stayed.
items.answer_should_show: An irrigation channel on one side bringing water. Water vapour rising from the field into the air. A white crust of salt on the soil. A drain at the far end carrying away some salt.

items.question: Draw a hill farm that saves both soil and water. Show at least three things the farmer does.
items.answer_should_show: Terraces or bunds across the slope, mulch between the rows, plants whose roots hold the soil, and a pond or tank at the bottom to catch the runoff.

items.question: Draw a leaf. Draw arrows for what goes in and what comes out. Then draw where the sugar goes.
items.answer_should_show: Arrows in for sunlight, water and carbon dioxide. An arrow out for oxygen. An arrow from the leaf down the stem to the roots, fruit or a growing tip, labelled sugar.

items.question: Draw yourself and a tree. Draw the gases that pass between you, with arrows and labels. Add the sunlight.
items.answer_should_show: An arrow from me to the tree labelled carbon dioxide. An arrow from the tree to me labelled oxygen. Sunlight shining on the tree's leaves.

items.question: Draw the journey of one carbon atom: from your breath, into a leaf, into a mango, into you, and back into the air.
items.answer_should_show: A loop of at least four pictures with arrows: a child breathing out, a leaf taking in carbon dioxide, a mango growing, the child eating the mango, and an arrow back to the breath.

items.question: Draw a graph showing how the oxygen in a pond changes from one afternoon to the next morning. Mark the highest point with a sun and the lowest point with a moon.
items.answer_should_show: A line that rises through the morning to a peak in the afternoon, then falls through the evening and night to its lowest point just before dawn. The sun is at the peak and the moon at the low point.

items.question: Draw the carbon cycle with at least five arrows. Include the air, a leaf, an animal, rotting and burning.
items.answer_should_show: Arrows from the air to a leaf (photosynthesis), from the leaf to an animal (eating), from the animal to the air (breathing), from dead leaves and animals to the air (rotting by fungi and bacteria), and from fuel to the air (burning).

items.question: Sketch what you would expect to find if you measured the oxygen around a pot plant in a sealed bag from 6 in the morning to 6 the next morning. Mark where the line crosses zero change.
items.answer_should_show: The oxygen rises from a low point in the morning as the light gets stronger. It crosses the compensation point shortly after dawn, peaks in the afternoon, falls through the evening and goes down all night.

items.question: Draw the cloth from your sprout test after you turned the cloth upside down. Draw the sprouts that held on.
items.answer_should_show: A cloth with most of the sprouts still hanging on it, and roots going into the cloth.

items.question: Draw a plant with all six parts: roots, stem, leaves, a flower, a fruit and seeds. Ask a grown-up to help you write the names.
items.answer_should_show: A plant with roots under a soil line, a stem, leaves, a flower, a fruit, and seeds inside the fruit.

items.question: Draw the moong cup on day 14, after you tipped the soil out. Draw the roots.
items.answer_should_show: A lump of soil in the shape of the cup, with white roots round the outside.

items.question: Draw the bowl of water from your float test. Draw each food where it really went: at the top or at the bottom.
items.answer_should_show: A bowl with brinjal, cucumber and the leaf at the top, and potato and chana at the bottom

items.question: Draw a banyan tree with three prop roots. Draw an arrow on one root to show which way it grew.
items.answer_should_show: A banyan with roots hanging down from the branches and arrows pointing down to the soil

items.question: Invent a plant that lives in a pond in a desert. Draw their roots, stem and leaves. Show one part that keeps water and one that brings air down.
items.answer_should_show: Any plant that has, for example, a fat stem for water and hollow stalks for air

items.question: Draw a plant with roots, a stem and leaves. Draw an arrow showing where water goes, and another showing where light comes from.
items.answer_should_show: Roots in the soil, a stem, and leaves spread out. A water arrow from the roots up the stem to the leaves. A light arrow from the Sun to the leaves.

items.question: Design the roots for a plant on a windy, rocky hillside. Draw them and label how they help.
items.answer_should_show: Deep roots pushing into cracks in the rock, and spreading side roots gripping the soil. Labels say they hold on against wind and reach water deep down.

items.question: Draw a zoom into a leaf in four steps: the leaf, its cells, the green blobs inside a cell, and a chlorophyll molecule catching light.
items.answer_should_show: A leaf. A wall of brick-like cells. Green blobs inside one cell. A ring-shaped molecule with a glowing photon arriving.

items.question: Draw your cup of moong shoots after one day by the window. Draw an arrow to show where the light came from.
items.answer_should_show: The cup with the shoots leaning towards the window, and an arrow from the window to the shoots.

items.question: Draw a moong shoot after one day by the window, then the same shoot one day after the cup was turned round.
items.answer_should_show: First a shoot leaning towards the window. Then a shoot bent like an S, the bottom leaning away and the top curving back to the window.

items.question: Imagine you turn the root box a quarter of the way round every day for three days. Draw the shape you think one root will make.
items.answer_should_show: A zigzag or a curl: each day the tip bends to point down again.

items.question: Draw one tree, one shrub and one herb. Show how their stems are different.
items.answer_should_show: A tree with one thick trunk, a shrub with many woody stems from the ground, and a small herb with a soft green stem.

items.question: Draw the view from your window or balcony. Mark one tree, one shrub, one herb and one climber or creeper, if you can see them. Label how you knew each kind.
items.answer_should_show: A drawing with plants labelled by kind, and a short clue for each, like 'one thick trunk' or 'soft green stem'.

items.question: Draw a forest with a tree, a climber, a shrub and a creeper. Draw arrows to show how each one reaches the sunlight.
items.answer_should_show: A tall tree reaching up, a climber climbing the tree, a shrub in a sunny gap and a creeper spreading in an open patch, each with an arrow to the sun.

items.question: Draw a money plant stem with two leaves. Label a node. Draw where new roots would grow on a cutting.
items.answer_should_show: A stem with two leaves, a node labelled where each leaf joins, and roots drawn coming from the node.

items.question: Draw the line graph from these Spice Guard results. Plain potato: day 2 is 0, day 3 is 2, day 4 is 5, day 5 is 9, day 6 is 12. Clove potato: 0 every day.
items.answer_should_show: Days 2 to 6 along the bottom, mouldy squares 0 to 16 up the side. One line climbing from 0 to 12, and one flat line at 0.

items.question: Design a sign for the gate of a sacred grove that tells visitors why the grove matters and what they must not do. Draw and write it.
items.answer_should_show: A sign with a picture of the grove and two or three reasons, such as old trees, rare plants, a spring, and rules like 'Do not cut or pick anything'.

items.question: Draw the underside of a fern frond. Show the brown dots and label 'frond' and 'sorus (spore dots)'.
items.answer_should_show: A frond with rows of dots underneath, labelled frond and sorus.

items.question: Use this table of features to draw a family tree of a moss, a fern, a pine and a mango. Moss: no veins, no seeds. Fern: veins, no seeds. Pine: veins, seeds, no flowers. Mango: veins, seeds, flowers.
items.answer_should_show: A trunk that splits first with the moss on one branch. Then the fern splits off. Then the pine. The mango is on the last branch.

items.question: Draw a plant in a pot. Draw blue arrows to show the path of water from the soil to the air. Label root, stem, leaf and air.
items.answer_should_show: Arrows start in the soil, go into the roots, up the stem, along the leaves, and out of the leaves into the air.

items.question: After the Blue Climb, a grown-up cuts across the flower's stem. Draw what you see at the cut end. Label the coloured dots and say what each dot is.
items.answer_should_show: A circle for the cut stem with a ring of coloured dots near the edge. A label says each dot is a bundle of xylem tubes that the coloured water climbed through.

items.question: Draw a tall tree with a chain of water inside from the roots to the leaves. Mark where the pull starts, where the Sun's energy comes in, and what holds the chain together.
items.answer_should_show: A tree with a line of water from the roots up the trunk to the leaves. An arrow shows vapour leaving a leaf hole at the top, labelled 'the pull starts here'. The Sun shines on the leaf, labelled 'energy'. The chain is labelled 'water molecules holding on to each other (cohesion)'.

items.question: Draw a cell in plain water and a cell in strong salt water. Use arrows to show which way water moves, and show how each cell looks.
items.answer_should_show: The first cell is plump with arrows pointing into it. The second is shrunken with arrows pointing out of it.

items.question: Draw a plant. Use arrows and labels to show where water enters, how it travels, and where it leaves. Label the root hairs, the xylem and a stoma.
items.answer_should_show: A plant with root hairs at the bottom with arrows in, a tube up the stem labelled xylem, and a stoma on a leaf with an arrow of vapour going out.

items.question: Draw a mangrove root standing in sea water. Show water drops going in and salt grains turned away at the root.
items.answer_should_show: A root in blue water with small drops passing into the root and salt dots stopped at the surface.

items.question: Draw the methi sprouts from under the bowl, and the methi sprouts from the window. Colour them the colours you saw.
items.answer_should_show: Tall, thin, yellow sprouts for the bowl. Short sprouts with green leaves for the window.

items.question: Draw a plant who has water but no light. Next to it, draw a plant who has light but no water.
items.answer_should_show: A tall, thin, yellow plant in damp soil, in a dark place. A droopy plant with dry soil in the sun.

items.question: Kalpana, a girl in Pune, puts a pot of sprouts inside a box with a hole on the left side. Draw how the sprouts will look in two days.
items.answer_should_show: The sprouts bend towards the hole on the left.

items.question: A cup of rai is turned round, and a day later turned round again. Each time, the tops bend to the light. Draw one stem from the side. How many new bends does it have?
items.answer_should_show: Two new bends, so the stem looks wiggly, like the letter S.

items.question: Draw the roots from a JUST RIGHT cup and from a SOAKED cup of the water test. Label two differences.
items.answer_should_show: The JUST RIGHT roots are white and spread out, with many tiny hairs. The SOAKED roots are brown and soft, with few hairs, and they smell bad.

items.question: Draw two seedlings: one grown in the light and one grown in the dark. Label three differences.
items.answer_should_show: The light seedling is short, thick and green, with open leaves. The dark seedling is tall, thin and pale yellow, bent over, with tiny folded leaves.

items.question: Draw a bar chart of the water test results: NONE 5 cm, JUST RIGHT 13 cm, SOAKED 8 cm. Label the bottom line and the side line.
items.answer_should_show: Three bars. NONE is 5 squares tall, JUST RIGHT is 13 and SOAKED is 8. The bottom line says 'Group' and the side line says 'Height (cm)'.

items.question: Draw the shortest-plank bucket for Zoya's moong in the dim window. Label each plank with a need. Make the shortest plank the need that held the moong back.
items.answer_should_show: A bucket with planks for light, water, air, warmth and minerals. The light plank is the shortest, and water spills out over it.

items.question: Draw a cutaway of a pot with soil grains, gaps and one root. Colour the air in the gaps one colour and water in the gaps another colour.
items.answer_should_show: Round grains in brown, white or blue gaps between them, a root running through the gaps with root hairs, air gaps shown in one colour and water in another, and a hole at the bottom of the pot.

items.question: Draw the root of a bean plant with nodules. Show the bacteria and add arrows for sugar and nitrogen.
items.answer_should_show: A root with small round lumps, one cut open to show bacteria inside, an arrow of sugar going from the plant into the nodule, and an arrow of nitrogen going from the nodule into the plant.

items.question: Draw a barrel with five planks labelled N, P, K, Ca and Fe, where nitrogen is the shortest. Draw what happens when a farmer adds potassium. Then draw what happens when she adds nitrogen.
items.answer_should_show: A barrel with the N plank shortest. After adding potassium the K plank is no different and the water level is still at N. After adding nitrogen the N plank is lengthened, and the water rises to the next shortest plank.

items.question: Draw the life cycle of a moong plant as a circle with arrows. Label each stage.
items.answer_should_show: A circle with five or six stages joined by arrows: seed, seedling, grown plant, flower, pod, and back to seed.

items.question: Cut a tomato across the middle. Draw what you see. Label the seeds, and the green star on top. What was the green star before the fruit grew?
items.answer_should_show: A circle with seeds in jelly, in two or more parts. The green star is labelled 'sepals'. They wrapped the flower bud before it opened.

items.question: Draw a bar chart of how long these plants take to go from sowing a seed to their first new seeds: moong 3 months, rice 4 months, tomato 4 months, papaya 10 months. Label the bottom line and the side line.
items.answer_should_show: Four bars. Moong 3 squares, rice 4, tomato 4, papaya 10. The bottom line says 'Plant' and the side line says 'Months'.

items.question: Draw the life cycle of a moong plant inside a bigger circle that shows where their atoms come from and go to: air, water, soil, and decomposers.
items.answer_should_show: An inner circle of seed, seedling, plant, flower, pod and seed. Around it, arrows from the air and the soil into the plant, and arrows from the dead plant through decomposers back to the air and soil.

items.question: Draw the life cycle of a fern as a circle with four pictures: a big fern with spore dots, a spore, a tiny heart-shaped plant and a baby fern. Join them with arrows.
items.answer_should_show: A circle of four pictures joined by arrows. A big fern with brown dots under its fronds leads to a spore. The spore leads to a tiny heart-shaped plant on damp soil. The heart-shaped plant leads to a baby fern, which grows into the big fern.

items.question: Draw a tree trunk cut across, showing about 10 rings. Make one ring very narrow and one very wide. Label the narrow ring with a likely cause, and the wide ring with a likely cause.
items.answer_should_show: A circle with about ten rings of different widths. The narrow ring is labelled drought or dry year. The wide ring is labelled good rain year.

items.question: Draw a timeline for a moong plant, a papaya plant and a mango tree. Use one centimetre for each year and mark how long each lives. Show what you notice about the moong plant.
items.answer_should_show: A line with marks at 0.25 centimetres for a moong plant, about 4 centimetres for a papaya plant and about 100 centimetres for a mango tree. The moong plant is a tiny speck.

items.question: Draw a chana seed under the soil on day 4. Show what is growing out of the seed.
items.answer_should_show: A seed with a long white root going down, and maybe a small curled shoot.

items.question: Draw a young plant. Show the root and the shoot, with an arrow for the way each one grows.
items.answer_should_show: The root with an arrow pointing down, the shoot with an arrow pointing up.

items.question: Draw a seed opened in half. Label the seed coat, the baby plant and the food store.
items.answer_should_show: A bean shape split open, with the coat peeling off, two large halves labelled 'food store' and a tiny plant at one edge labelled 'baby plant'.

items.question: Draw the seed window jar after 5 days. Show 3 seeds that started in different ways, with their roots and shoots.
items.answer_should_show: Three seeds, each with a root curving down and a shoot curving up, whichever way the seed was placed.

items.question: Invent a seed for a desert where rain falls only once every few years. Draw them and label two features that help them wait and then sprout fast.
items.answer_should_show: Any thoughtful design, for example: a very hard waterproof coat so they can wait for years, a coat that only softens after lots of rain, a big food store so the root can grow fast and deep.

items.question: Draw a waking curve for a plate of 30 seeds. Put the hours along the bottom and the number of seeds with a root up the side. Show a lazy S shape, and mark where about half the seeds had woken.
items.answer_should_show: A line graph with hours along the bottom and seeds with a root up the side. The line starts low, climbs steeply in the middle and flattens near the top. A mark is on the line where it reaches about 15 seeds.

items.question: Draw two moong or chana seedlings in cutaway soil. On one, show the seed leaves lifted into the air. On the other, show them left under the soil. Label which is which.
items.answer_should_show: Two cutaway pictures. In the first, a hooked stem has pulled two fat green seed leaves above the soil line. In the second, the seed leaves are still buried and only a shoot with small leaves is above the soil.

items.question: Here are made-up counts of seeds with a root. At 12 hours: 3 seeds. At 24 hours: 12. At 36 hours: 20. At 48 hours: 22. Draw the line graph. Put the hours along the bottom and the seeds with a root up the side.
items.answer_should_show: A line graph with points at (12, 3), (24, 12), (36, 20) and (48, 22). The line climbs steeply from 12 to 36 hours and flattens between 36 and 48 hours.

items.question: In the Smell Steps test, you walked towards a peeled orange with your eyes shut. Draw where you were when you first smelled the orange.
items.answer_should_show: A drawing of the child a few steps from the plate, with their hand raised.

items.question: Draw your favourite food. Around it, draw each sense organ that can tell you something about it.
items.answer_should_show: A food with several sense organs drawn around it, such as an eye, a nose and a tongue.

items.question: Draw an ant walking to a grain of sugar. Draw the smell trail she follows, and the feelers she smells with.
items.answer_should_show: An ant with two feelers on her head, a trail of tiny dots on the ground, and a sugar grain at the end.

items.question: Draw the path of a smell: from a bowl of hot payasam, up your nose, to your brain. Label the smell molecules, the smell receptors and the nerve.
items.answer_should_show: Molecules float from the payasam into the nose. They reach receptor cells high inside the nose. A nerve carries the signal to the brain.

items.question: Draw the same mango three ways: as you see it, as a dog might smell the mango, and as a fly might taste it with their feet.
items.answer_should_show: Any drawing that shows the mango in three different sense-worlds: colours for you, smell clouds for the dog, and taste spots under the fly's feet.

items.question: Draw a nerve thread with three pulses for a light touch and ten pulses for a hard press. Label which is which.
items.answer_should_show: Two threads of the same length. The first has three small identical sparks along it, labelled light touch. The second has ten identical sparks, labelled hard press. The sparks are all the same size.

items.question: Draw two bags in a child's hands, one light and one heavy. Show how much extra weight is needed to feel a difference in each.
items.answer_should_show: A small bag with a small extra and a big bag with a bigger extra, in the same share. For example, 10 grams on a 100 gram bag and 100 grams on a 1 kilogram bag.

items.question: Draw a timeline of a falling ruler: when it starts to fall, when the light reaches the eye, when the signal reaches the brain and when the fingers close. Mark which gap is longest.
items.answer_should_show: A line with four marks in order. The first two marks are almost at the same place because light is very fast. The signal reaches the brain a little later. The fingers close last. The longest gap is from the eye or brain to the fingers closing.

items.question: A bowl of water with a paper arrow floating on it is spun round, then stopped suddenly. Draw the bowl just after it stops. Show with arrows what the water is doing.
items.answer_should_show: A still bowl, with curved arrows showing the water and the paper arrow still turning.

items.question: Draw two hands: one on a steel plate and one on a wooden board. Use arrows to show the heat leaving each hand. Make the arrows bigger where more heat leaves.
items.answer_should_show: Big arrows from the hand into the steel, small arrows from the hand into the wood.

items.question: Draw a cartoon strip of four pictures showing how a fish's lateral line helps them escape a hunter in muddy water.
items.answer_should_show: 1. A fish in muddy water. 2. A bigger fish coming from behind, out of sight. 3. Water pushed ahead of the hunter reaching the fish's side. 4. The fish darting away.

items.question: Draw a child's head and body. Draw three lines that carry messages to the brain from the eyes, the inner ears and the feet. Label each line with what it tells the brain.
items.answer_should_show: A child with three lines going to the head: from the eyes (where the horizon is), from the ears (turning and tilting), and from the feet (what the ground is like).

items.question: Draw a loop of four arrows that shows how the body keeps its temperature steady when you get too warm. Label each arrow.
items.answer_should_show: A loop: sensors in the skin and body feel the warmth, the brain compares it with the level it aims for, the body sweats and widens its skin blood vessels, and the temperature falls and is sensed again.

items.question: Draw your family's night path to the toilet. Mark with arrows where the eyes, the feet and a light fingertip get help.
items.answer_should_show: A plan of the path with a low light for the eyes, a rough strip or handrail for the fingertip, and a firm mat or ridged floor for the feet.

items.question: Draw the arrow lines: one 6 cm line with arrowheads and one 6 cm line with open fins. Use a ruler. Circle the one that looks longer.
items.answer_should_show: Two 6 cm lines, one <——> and one >——<. The open-fin line is circled.

items.question: Draw a shaded circle that looks like a bump, and one that looks like a dent. Draw a small Sun to show where the light seems to come from.
items.answer_should_show: The bump is light at the top and dark at the bottom. The dent is dark at the top and light at the bottom. The Sun is drawn above.

items.question: Invent your own illusion using one of the clues: far away, neighbours or light from above. Draw it and write the question you would ask a visitor.
items.answer_should_show: Any drawing that uses one clue correctly, with a clear question, for example two equal lines between two walls of a corridor drawn in perspective, with the question 'Which person is taller?'.

items.question: Draw three black circles with a slice missing from each. Arrange them so that a triangle appears between them. Draw a dotted line where the brain adds the edge.
items.answer_should_show: Three circles at the corners of a triangle with the missing slices pointing to the middle, and dotted lines joining the slices where the triangle's edges are seen.

items.question: Draw a tick on a leaf. Show with clouds, arrows or colour what is in the tick's world, and leave the rest of the page blank.
items.answer_should_show: A tick on a leaf with small clouds of sweat smell and heat lines coming from an animal, and little else.

items.question: Draw a shape that can be read as two different things. Label the two readings.
items.answer_should_show: A shape such as a curved line that can be a banana or a boat, with both readings labelled.

items.question: Draw a rocket going up. Draw an arrow to show which way the hot gas goes, and another arrow to show which way the rocket goes.
items.answer_should_show: A rocket with a big arrow pointing down out of its engine for the gas, and a big arrow pointing up on the rocket.

items.question: Draw what you saw in the half-lens test, two times: with the whole lens open, and with half of it covered. Shade them to show the brightness.
items.answer_should_show: Two pictures of the whole window, upside down. The second is shaded darker but is complete.

items.question: Draw a Moon home with an airlock. Show the two doors and where the astronaut stands between them.
items.answer_should_show: A sealed home with a small room on one side. The small room has an inner door into the home and an outer door to the Moon. The astronaut stands in the small room with both doors shut.

items.question: Draw Newton's cannon on a high mountain. Show three paths of the cannonball: one that lands near, one that lands far, and one that goes right round the Earth.
items.answer_should_show: A mountain on a round Earth, with a short curved path, a longer curved path, and a path that circles the whole Earth.

items.question: Draw a satellite going round the Earth. Draw an arrow for the way it is moving and an arrow for the pull of gravity.
items.answer_should_show: A circle for the Earth and a satellite on the circle's edge. One arrow along the path, sideways. One arrow pointing from the satellite towards the middle of the Earth.

items.question: Draw a radio dish with some waves coming in from space. Show where the waves go after they hit the dish, and where the receiver sits.
items.answer_should_show: A curved dish facing upwards with parallel lines coming in, bending to meet at one point above the dish. The receiver is drawn at that point.

items.question: Draw your sinking cup clock floating in the vessel. Label the hole, the coins, the water coming in, and the water in the vessel.
items.answer_should_show: A cup floating in a larger vessel, with coins taped inside at the bottom, a small hole in the bottom, an arrow showing water coming up through the hole, and the water level of the vessel.

items.question: Draw a stick and its noon shadow in Chennai, and the same stick and its noon shadow in Delhi on a day in January. Show which shadow is longer.
items.answer_should_show: Two sticks of the same height. The Delhi shadow is longer than the Chennai shadow, because Delhi is further north and the Sun is lower in its sky at noon.

items.question: Design a water clock that shows each minute with a mark, so you can read the time without counting sinkings. Draw it and label the parts.
items.answer_should_show: For example, a tall clear bottle filled slowly by a dripping cup above, with lines on the side marked 1, 2, 3 minutes, made by timing the rising water. Or a floating stick rising in a pot as it fills, pointing to marks.

items.question: Draw an ellipse that you made with two pins. Mark the two pins and label one of them 'Sun'.
items.answer_should_show: An oval with two dots inside it on the long line, one of them labelled Sun.

items.question: Draw the lamp and the ball. Show where the ball must be to look nearly full when seen from the chair.
items.answer_should_show: A lamp in the middle, a chair on one side, and a ball on the far side of the lamp from the chair, a little off the line.

items.question: Draw the Sun with two orbits round it, the Earth on the inner orbit and Mars on the outer one. Show where the Earth is when it overtakes Mars.
items.answer_should_show: The Sun in the middle with a small orbit and a larger orbit. The Earth and Mars are on the same side of the Sun, with the Earth on the inner orbit between the Sun and Mars.

items.question: Draw a cup of sea water that is half frozen. Show where the ice is, and where the salt has gone.
items.answer_should_show: Ice on top, almost without salt. Salty leftover water underneath, with the salt drawn as dots crowded in the liquid.

items.question: Draw a tardigrade in moss in the rainy season, and the same tardigrade in summer when the moss is dry.
items.answer_should_show: In the rain, a tardigrade walking on eight stubby legs in wet moss. In summer, the tardigrade curled into a small dry ball with no legs showing.

items.question: Draw a model of a sea-ice channel with microbes living in it. Show the ice, the salty liquid, and what the microbes need.
items.answer_should_show: Ice crystals on both sides, a thin channel of brine between them, microbes in the liquid, and labels for liquid water, energy and chemicals.

items.question: Draw the four bottles of the yeast test with their balloons at the end. Show which balloon is big and which are flat. Label the bottles that hold life.
items.answer_should_show: Four bottles. The balloon on the bottle with yeast and sugar is large. The balloons on the bottle with yeast only, the bottle with sugar only and the bottle with dead yeast are flat or almost flat. Only the first is labelled as holding life.

items.question: Draw a star with a planet crossing in front of it. Below it, draw a graph of the star's brightness over time. Mark the dip, and mark the length of the planet's year.
items.answer_should_show: A star with a small planet in front of it. Below, a flat line with a small dip, and a second dip later. An arrow between the two dips labelled the planet's year.

items.question: Draw the habitable zone around a bright star and around a dim red star. Put a planet in the zone of each.
items.answer_should_show: Two stars. The bright star has a ring that is far out, with a planet in it. The dim red star has a ring that is very close in, with a planet in it. A note says the dim star's zone is much closer.

items.question: Draw the Moon on the night of your favourite Moon festival. Write the festival's name and whether it is Amavasya or Purnima.
items.answer_should_show: For example, Diwali: a dark sky with no Moon, because it is Amavasya. Or Karthigai Deepam: a full round Moon, because it is Purnima.

items.question: Draw a lunar eclipse from the side: the Sun, the Earth with its shadow, and the Moon inside the shadow. Label each one.
items.answer_should_show: The Sun on one side, the Earth in the middle, a long dark shadow behind the Earth, and the Moon inside that shadow, all in a straight line.

items.question: Design a Moon base on the far side of the Moon. Show how it would talk to the Earth.
items.answer_should_show: Any design that includes a relay satellite or another way to send messages round the Moon.

items.question: Draw a half Moon with a crater near the line between light and dark. Draw its shadow, and show which way the Sun is.
items.answer_should_show: A half Moon lit on the right, with a crater near the middle line. The shadow inside the crater is on the side facing the dark. An arrow shows the Sun on the lit side.

items.question: Draw the Sun, the Earth and the Moon in a line at new Moon. Draw the sea on the Earth with a bulge facing the Moon and a bulge on the other side.
items.answer_should_show: The Sun on one side, the Moon in the middle, the Earth on the other side, and two bulges of water on the Earth along the line.

items.question: Draw a growing half Moon as it looks from Australia, and say which side is lit.
items.answer_should_show: A half Moon lit on the left. The lit side faces the Sun, but the Moon appears upside down compared with India.

items.question: Draw the Sun and a comet at two places on its path: one coming in towards the Sun and one going away. Draw each comet's tail.
items.answer_should_show: Both tails point straight away from the Sun. The coming-in comet has its tail behind it, and the going-away comet has its tail in front.

items.question: Draw the Earth's round path and a comet's long, stretched path crossing it. Show where the comet's dust is, and where the Earth will see a meteor shower.
items.answer_should_show: A circle for the Earth's path, a long oval for the comet's path crossing it, dots of dust along the oval, and a mark at the crossing for the meteor shower.

items.question: Draw a comet at three places on its path: far out, coming close to the Sun, and nearest the Sun. Show how its tail changes.
items.answer_should_show: Far out: a small dark lump, no tail. Coming close: a small coma and a short tail. Nearest the Sun: a big coma and a long tail. Every tail points away from the Sun.

items.question: Draw the Sun and the first four planets, with the Earth in the right place. Draw an arrow to show which way the Sun's gravity pulls the Earth.
